--!strict
-- Sb16.lua -- practical ISA Sound Blaster 16 subset.
--
-- DSP reset/commands, mixer registers, FM register latches and 8-bit DMA
-- playback are modelled. FM synthesis and audio mixing are host concerns; the
-- injected sink receives the raw unsigned 8-bit sample block. Playback is
-- pumped synchronously or by the machine's periodic tick.

const band, bor, lshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift

const DEFAULT_BASE = 0x220
const DEFAULT_IRQ = 5
const DEFAULT_DMA = 1

const PARAM_COUNTS: { [number]: number } = {
	[0x10] = 1, -- direct DAC
	[0x14] = 2, -- single-cycle 8-bit DMA
	[0x1C] = 2, -- auto-init 8-bit DMA
	[0x40] = 1, -- time constant
	[0x41] = 2, -- sample rate
	[0x48] = 2, -- block size
}

export type Config = {
	base: number?,
	irq: number?,
	dma: any?,
	dmaChannel: number?,
	sink: ((samples: buffer) -> ())?,
}

const Sb16 = {}
Sb16.__index = Sb16

export type Sb16 = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		base: number,
		irq: number,
		dma: any?,
		dmaChannel: number,
		sink: (samples: buffer) -> (),
		resetHeld: boolean,
		readQueue: { number },
		readHead: number,
		pendingCommand: number?,
		pendingParams: { number },
		pendingNeeded: number,
		versionMajor: number,
		versionMinor: number,
		mixerAddress: number,
		mixerRegs: { [number]: number },
		fmAddress: number,
		fmRegs: { [number]: number },
		speakerOn: boolean,
		timeConstant: number,
		sampleRate: number,
		blockSize: number,
		remaining: number,
		active: boolean,
		autoinit: boolean,
		paused: boolean,
		irqPending: boolean,
		lastCommand: number,
		lastDac: number,
		in8: (self: Sb16, port: number) -> number,
		out8: (self: Sb16, port: number, value: number) -> (),
		resetDsp: (self: Sb16) -> (),
		executeCommand: (self: Sb16, command: number, params: { number }) -> (),
		takeIrq: (self: Sb16) -> boolean,
		pump: (self: Sb16) -> number,
		tick: (self: Sb16) -> number,
	},
	Sb16
))

local function clearQueue(self: Sb16)
	self.readQueue = {}
	self.readHead = 1
end

local function queueByte(self: Sb16, value: number)
	self.readQueue[#self.readQueue + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
end

local function hasData(self: Sb16): boolean
	return self.readHead <= #self.readQueue
end

local function dspRead(self: Sb16): number
	if not hasData(self) then
		return 0xFF
	end
	const value = self.readQueue[self.readHead]
	self.readHead += 1
	if self.readHead > #self.readQueue then
		clearQueue(self)
	end
	return value
end

local function resetMixer(self: Sb16)
	self.mixerRegs = {}
	self.mixerAddress = 0
end

function Sb16.new(config: Config?): Sb16
	const cfg = (config or {}) :: Config
	local self = setmetatable({}, Sb16) :: any
	self.base = cfg.base or DEFAULT_BASE
	self.irq = cfg.irq or DEFAULT_IRQ
	self.dma = cfg.dma
	self.dmaChannel = cfg.dmaChannel or DEFAULT_DMA
	self.sink = cfg.sink or function() end
	self.versionMajor = 4
	self.versionMinor = 5
	self.mixerRegs = {}
	self.mixerAddress = 0
	self.fmRegs = {}
	self.fmAddress = 0
	self.lastCommand = 0
	self.lastDac = 0
	self:resetDsp()
	return self
end

function Sb16.resetDsp(self: Sb16)
	clearQueue(self)
	self.resetHeld = false
	self.pendingCommand = nil
	self.pendingParams = {}
	self.pendingNeeded = 0
	self.speakerOn = false
	self.timeConstant = 0
	self.sampleRate = 0
	self.blockSize = 0
	self.remaining = 0
	self.active = false
	self.autoinit = false
	self.paused = false
	self.irqPending = false
	self.lastDac = 0
	if self.dma then
		self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, false)
	end
	queueByte(self, 0xAA)
end

function Sb16.takeIrq(self: Sb16): boolean
	if not self.irqPending then
		return false
	end
	self.irqPending = false
	return true
end

local function dspWrite(self: Sb16, value: number)
	value = band(value, 0xFF)
	if self.pendingNeeded > 0 then
		self.pendingParams[#self.pendingParams + 1] = value
		self.pendingNeeded -= 1
		if self.pendingNeeded == 0 then
			const command = self.pendingCommand
			const params = self.pendingParams
			self.pendingCommand = nil
			self.pendingParams = {}
			if command ~= nil then
				self:executeCommand(command, params)
			end
		end
		return
	end
	self.lastCommand = value
	const needed = PARAM_COUNTS[value] or 0
	if needed == 0 then
		self:executeCommand(value, {})
	else
		self.pendingCommand = value
		self.pendingParams = {}
		self.pendingNeeded = needed
	end
end

function Sb16.executeCommand(self: Sb16, command: number, params: { number })
	if command == 0xE1 then
		queueByte(self, self.versionMajor)
		queueByte(self, self.versionMinor)
	elseif command == 0x10 then
		self.lastDac = params[1] or 0
		if self.speakerOn then
			const sample = buffer.create(1)
			buffer.writeu8(sample, 0, self.lastDac)
			self.sink(sample)
		end
	elseif command == 0x14 or command == 0x1C then
		const length = bor(params[1] or 0, lshift(params[2] or 0, 8))
		self.blockSize = length + 1
		self.autoinit = command == 0x1C
		self.remaining = self.blockSize
		self.active = true
		self.paused = false
		self.irqPending = false
		if self.dma then
			self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, true)
		end
		self:pump()
	elseif command == 0x40 then
		self.timeConstant = params[1] or 0
		if self.timeConstant < 256 then
			self.sampleRate = math.floor(1000000 / (256 - self.timeConstant) + 0.5)
		else
			self.sampleRate = 0
		end
	elseif command == 0x41 then
		self.sampleRate = bor(lshift(params[1] or 0, 8), params[2] or 0)
	elseif command == 0x48 then
		self.blockSize = bor(params[1] or 0, lshift(params[2] or 0, 8)) + 1
	elseif command == 0xD0 then
		self.paused = true
	elseif command == 0xD1 then
		self.speakerOn = true
	elseif command == 0xD3 then
		self.speakerOn = false
	elseif command == 0xD4 then
		self.paused = false
	elseif command == 0xDA then
		self.autoinit = false
		self.active = false
		if self.dma then
			self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, false)
		end
	end
end

function Sb16.pump(self: Sb16): number
	if not self.active or self.paused or not self.dma then
		return 0
	end
	if self.remaining <= 0 then
		return 0
	end
	const samples = self.dma:read(self.dmaChannel, self.remaining)
	if not samples or buffer.len(samples) == 0 then
		if not self.autoinit then
			self.active = false
			self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, false)
		end
		return 0
	end
	const count = buffer.len(samples)
	if self.speakerOn then
		self.sink(samples)
	end
	self.remaining -= count
	if self.remaining <= 0 then
		self.irqPending = true
		if self.autoinit then
			self.remaining = self.blockSize
			self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, true)
		else
			self.active = false
			self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, false)
		end
	end
	return count
end

function Sb16.tick(self: Sb16): number
	return self:pump()
end

function Sb16.in8(self: Sb16, port: number): number
	if port == self.base + 4 then
		return self.mixerAddress
	elseif port == self.base + 5 then
		return self.mixerRegs[self.mixerAddress] or 0
	elseif port == self.base + 6 then
		return 0xFF
	elseif port == self.base + 8 or port == 0x388 then
		return 0 -- FM timer status: no expired timers
	elseif port == self.base + 9 or port == 0x389 then
		return self.fmRegs[self.fmAddress] or 0
	elseif port == self.base + 0x0A then
		return dspRead(self)
	elseif port == self.base + 0x0E then
		return if hasData(self) then 0x80 else 0x00
	end
	return 0xFF
end

function Sb16.out8(self: Sb16, port: number, value: number)
	value = band(value, 0xFF)
	if port == self.base + 4 then
		self.mixerAddress = value
	elseif port == self.base + 5 then
		if self.mixerAddress == 0 then
			resetMixer(self)
		else
			self.mixerRegs[self.mixerAddress] = value
		end
	elseif port == self.base + 6 then
		if band(value, 1) ~= 0 then
			self.resetHeld = true
			clearQueue(self)
			self.pendingCommand = nil
			self.pendingParams = {}
			self.pendingNeeded = 0
			self.active = false
			if self.dma then
				self.dma:request(self.dmaChannel, false)
			end
		elseif self.resetHeld then
			self:resetDsp()
		end
	elseif port == self.base + 8 or port == 0x388 then
		self.fmAddress = value
	elseif port == self.base + 9 or port == 0x389 then
		self.fmRegs[self.fmAddress] = value
	elseif port == self.base + 0x0C then
		dspWrite(self, value)
	end
end

return Sb16

--!strict
-- Checks of an operation's fields, shared by every operation: each refuses with the reason.

local Errors = require("../../Core/Errors")
local Store = require("./Store")

local Need = {}

local function isFinite(value: any): boolean
	return type(value) == "number" and value == value and math.abs(value) ~= math.huge
end

local function milliseconds(time: number): number
	return math.round(time * 1000) / 1000
end

local function rounded(value: number, places: number): number
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.round(value * scale) / scale
end

local function refuse(where: string, message: string, hint: string?): never
	return Errors.throw("INVALID_ARGUMENT", `{where}: {message}`, hint)
end

local function needTime(where: string, value: any, field: string)
	if not isFinite(value) or value < 0 or value > Store.MAX_TIME then
		refuse(where, `{field} must be from 0 to {Store.MAX_TIME} seconds.`)
	end
end

local function needJoint(where: string, name: any, joints: { [string]: any })
	if type(name) ~= "string" or not joints[name] then
		refuse(where, `the rig has no joint "{tostring(name)}".`, "Call inspect_rig for the joint names.")
	end
end

local function needVector(where: string, value: any, field: string, limit: number?)
	if value == nil then
		return
	end
	if type(value) ~= "table" or #value ~= 3 then
		refuse(where, `{field} must be three numbers.`)
	end
	for index = 1, 3 do
		if not isFinite(value[index]) or (limit and math.abs(value[index]) > limit) then
			refuse(where, `{field} must be three finite numbers{if limit then ` within {limit}` else ""}.`)
		end
	end
end

-- With `wraps`, time_from may be after time_to: in a looping clip the range then runs on
-- past the end and round from the start (see Seam).
local function needRange(where: string, operation: any, wraps: boolean?)
	needTime(where, operation.time_from, "time_from")
	needTime(where, operation.time_to, "time_to")
	if operation.time_to < operation.time_from and not wraps then
		refuse(where, "time_to must not be before time_from.")
	end
end

local function needJoints(where: string, list: any, joints: { [string]: any })
	if list == nil then
		return
	end
	if type(list) ~= "table" or #list == 0 or #list > Store.MAX_JOINTS then
		refuse(where, `joints must list from 1 to {Store.MAX_JOINTS} joint names.`)
	end
	for _, name in list do
		needJoint(where, name, joints)
	end
end

local function needOneOf(where: string, value: any, field: string, allowed: { string })
	if type(value) ~= "string" or not table.find(allowed, value) then
		refuse(where, `{field} must be one of {table.concat(allowed, ", ")}.`)
	end
end

local function needText(where: string, value: any, field: string, limit: number, allowEmpty: boolean?)
	if type(value) ~= "string" or #value > limit or (not allowEmpty and #value == 0) then
		refuse(where, `{field} must be text of {if allowEmpty then "at most" else "1 to"} {limit} characters.`)
	end
end

local function needBlends(where: string, operation: any)
	for _, field in { "blend_in", "blend_out" } do
		local value = operation[field]
		if value ~= nil and (not isFinite(value) or value < 0 or value > Store.MAX_BLEND) then
			refuse(where, `{field} must be from 0 to {Store.MAX_BLEND} seconds.`)
		end
	end
end

Need.isFinite = isFinite
Need.milliseconds = milliseconds
Need.rounded = rounded
Need.refuse = refuse
Need.needTime = needTime
Need.needJoint = needJoint
Need.needVector = needVector
Need.needRange = needRange
Need.needJoints = needJoints
Need.needOneOf = needOneOf
Need.needText = needText
Need.needBlends = needBlends

return Need

--!strict
-- Snapshot.lua -- delta checkpoints of a whole Machine.
--
-- A machine is a graph of plain tables, scalars and buffers plus methods that
-- live on metatables and on instance fields (closures). Saving closures is
-- not possible, so a checkpoint is a *delta against a freshly built machine*:
-- the caller supplies a factory that builds the same machine (same ROMs, same
-- base disk images, same config) and capture() walks the live graph and the
-- fresh one in lock-step, recording only scalar fields that differ, tables the
-- fresh machine lacks, and 4 KiB pages of buffers that differ. apply() builds
-- nothing itself: it overlays that delta onto another fresh machine, leaving
-- every function (including instance-patched ones) untouched.
--
-- Not captured: functions, metatables, userdata other than buffers, tables
-- used as keys. State that lives only in a closure's upvalues is therefore not
-- captured; the determinism test in tests/SnapshotTests.lua is the check that
-- a given machine configuration has none.

local Snapshot = {}

local PAGE = 4096
local MAGIC = "RVPCSNAP1"
local ZERO_PAGE = string.rep("\0", PAGE)

local pack = string.pack
-- string.unpack is typed as returning unknowns; every format used here yields
-- numbers (the one string result is only passed through as `any`).
local unpack = string.unpack :: (fmt: string, s: string, init: number?) -> ...number

local encodeValue: (v: any, out: { string }, seen: { [any]: boolean }) -> ()

local function encodeBuffer(b: buffer, out: { string })
	local len = buffer.len(b)
	local pages: { string } = {}
	local count = 0
	local off = 0
	while off < len do
		local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
		local s = buffer.readstring(b, off, n)
		if s ~= string.sub(ZERO_PAGE, 1, n) then
			count += 1
			pages[#pages + 1] = pack("<I4", off // PAGE)
			pages[#pages + 1] = s
		end
		off += PAGE
	end
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I4I4", len, count)
	for _, p in pages do
		out[#out + 1] = p
	end
end

function encodeValue(v: any, out: { string }, seen: { [any]: boolean })
	local t = typeof(v)
	if t == "boolean" then
		out[#out + 1] = if v then "T" else "F"
	elseif t == "number" then
		out[#out + 1] = "N" .. pack("<d", v)
	elseif t == "string" then
		out[#out + 1] = "S" .. pack("<s4", v)
	elseif t == "buffer" then
		out[#out + 1] = "B"
		encodeBuffer(v, out)
	elseif t == "table" then
		if seen[v] then
			error("snapshot: cycle inside a table the fresh machine does not have")
		end
		seen[v] = true
		local keys: { { any } } = {}
		for k, val in v do
			local kt = typeof(k)
			local vt = typeof(val)
			if
				(kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean")
				and vt ~= "function"
				and vt ~= "thread"
				and vt ~= "userdata"
				and vt ~= "vector"
			then
				keys[#keys + 1] = { k, val }
			end
		end
		out[#out + 1] = "{" .. pack("<I4", #keys)
		for _, kv in keys do
			encodeValue(kv[1], out, seen)
			encodeValue(kv[2], out, seen)
		end
		seen[v] = nil
	else
		out[#out + 1] = "Z"
	end
end

local decodeValue: (data: string, pos: number) -> (any, number)

function decodeValue(data: string, pos: number): (any, number)
	local tag = string.sub(data, pos, pos)
	pos += 1
	if tag == "Z" then
		return nil, pos
	elseif tag == "T" then
		return true, pos
	elseif tag == "F" then
		return false, pos
	elseif tag == "N" then
		local n, p = unpack("<d", data, pos)
		return n, p
	elseif tag == "S" then
		local s, p = unpack("<s4", data, pos)
		return s, p
	elseif tag == "B" then
		local len, count = unpack("<I4I4", data, pos)
		pos += 8
		local b = buffer.create(len)
		for _ = 1, count do
			local idx = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
			pos += 4
			local off = idx * PAGE
			local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
			buffer.writestring(b, off, string.sub(data, pos, pos + n - 1))
			pos += n
		end
		return b, pos
	elseif tag == "{" then
		local count = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
		pos += 4
		local t: { [any]: any } = {}
		for _ = 1, count do
			local k, v
			k, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			v, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			t[k] = v
		end
		return t, pos
	end
	error("snapshot: bad value tag at " .. tostring(pos - 1))
end

local function encodePath(path: { any }, out: { string })
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I2", #path)
	for _, key in path do
		encodeValue(key, out, {})
	end
end

local function emitSet(path: { any }, value: any, out: { string })
	out[#out + 1] = "V"
	encodePath(path, out)
	encodeValue(value, out, {})
end

local function emitBufferDiff(path: { any }, live: buffer, ref: buffer, out: { string })
	local len = buffer.len(live)
	local pages: { string } = {}
	local count = 0
	local off = 0
	while off < len do
		local n = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
		local s = buffer.readstring(live, off, n)
		if s ~= buffer.readstring(ref, off, n) then
			count += 1
			pages[#pages + 1] = pack("<I4", off // PAGE)
			pages[#pages + 1] = s
		end
		off += PAGE
	end
	if count == 0 then
		return
	end
	out[#out + 1] = "D"
	encodePath(path, out)
	out[#out + 1] = pack("<I4I4", len, count)
	for _, p in pages do
		out[#out + 1] = p
	end
end

local function skippable(vt: string): boolean
	return vt == "function" or vt == "thread" or vt == "userdata" or vt == "vector"
end

local function walk(
	live: any,
	ref: any,
	path: { any },
	out: { string },
	visited: { [any]: boolean }
)
	for k, v in live do
		local kt = typeof(k)
		if kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean" then
			local vt = typeof(v)
			path[#path + 1] = k
			if vt == "table" then
				if not visited[v] then
					visited[v] = true
					local r = ref[k]
					if typeof(r) == "table" then
						walk(v, r, path, out, visited)
					else
						emitSet(path, v, out)
					end
				end
			elseif vt == "buffer" then
				if not visited[v] then
					visited[v] = true
					local r = ref[k]
					if typeof(r) == "buffer" and buffer.len(r) == buffer.len(v) then
						emitBufferDiff(path, v, r, out)
					else
						emitSet(path, v, out)
					end
				end
			elseif not skippable(vt) then
				if ref[k] ~= v then
					emitSet(path, v, out)
				end
			end
			path[#path] = nil
		end
	end
	for k, r in ref do
		local kt = typeof(k)
		if (kt == "string" or kt == "number" or kt == "boolean") and live[k] == nil then
			if not skippable(typeof(r)) then
				path[#path + 1] = k
				emitSet(path, nil, out)
				path[#path] = nil
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Records how `live` differs from `ref` (a machine freshly built the same way).
-- `extra` is any plain-data table the caller wants stored alongside (driver
-- state such as step counters); apply() hands it back.
function Snapshot.capture(live: any, ref: any, extra: any?): string
	local out: { string } = { MAGIC }
	encodeValue(extra or {}, out, {})
	walk(live, ref, {}, out, { [live] = true })
	return table.concat(out)
end

local function resolve(root: any, path: { any }): any
	local t = root
	for i = 1, #path - 1 do
		local nxt = t[path[i]]
		if typeof(nxt) ~= "table" then
			error("snapshot: path does not exist in the fresh machine")
		end
		t = nxt
	end
	return t
end

-- Overlays a checkpoint onto `target`, a machine built exactly like the
-- reference was. Returns the `extra` table that was captured.
function Snapshot.apply(target: any, data: string): any
	if string.sub(data, 1, #MAGIC) ~= MAGIC then
		error("snapshot: bad header")
	end
	local pos = #MAGIC + 1
	local extra
	extra, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
	local size = #data
	while pos <= size do
		local tag = string.sub(data, pos, pos)
		pos += 1
		local n = unpack("<I2", data, pos)
		pos += 2
		local path: { any } = {}
		for i = 1, n do
			path[i], pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
		end
		local parent = resolve(target, path)
		local key = path[#path]
		if tag == "V" then
			local v
			v, pos = decodeValue(data, pos)
			parent[key] = v
		elseif tag == "D" then
			local len, count = unpack("<I4I4", data, pos)
			pos += 8
			local b = parent[key]
			if typeof(b) ~= "buffer" or buffer.len(b) ~= len then
				error(
					"snapshot: buffer mismatch against the fresh machine at "
						.. table.concat(path, ".")
						.. " (len "
						.. tostring(len)
						.. " vs "
						.. (if typeof(b) == "buffer" then tostring(buffer.len(b)) else typeof(b))
						.. ")"
				)
			end
			for _ = 1, count do
				local idx = unpack("<I4", data, pos)
				pos += 4
				local off = idx * PAGE
				local len2 = math.min(PAGE, len - off)
				buffer.writestring(b, off, string.sub(data, pos, pos + len2 - 1))
				pos += len2
			end
		else
			error("snapshot: bad op tag at " .. tostring(pos - 3))
		end
	end
	return extra
end

return Snapshot

--!strict
-- Moving a hand or foot off its own path for a few frames, by an offset that eases in and
-- out: a kicking foot lifted at the chamber, a punch carried a little higher. Unlike pin,
-- which holds the part at one point, the part keeps travelling along its own motion,
-- moved by the offset, so a fast limb is not dragged back toward where a pin held it.

local Frames = require("./Frames")
local Body = require("./Body")
local Limb = require("../../Rigs/Limb")
local Need = require("./Need")
local Pose = require("../../Rigs/Pose")
local Rig = require("../../Rigs/Rig")
local Roblox = require("../../Core/Roblox")
local Store = require("./Store")
local Write = require("./Write")

local count = Frames.count
local FRAME_SLACK = Frames.FRAME_SLACK
local hasGeometry = Body.hasGeometry
local isFinite = Need.isFinite
local milliseconds = Need.milliseconds
local needBlends = Need.needBlends
local needJoint = Need.needJoint
local needOneOf = Need.needOneOf
local needRange = Need.needRange
local readChannels = Frames.readChannels
local refuse = Need.refuse
local rounded = Need.rounded
local smoothstep = Frames.smoothstep
local transformsAt = Frames.transformsAt
local writeTurns = Write.writeTurns

type Changed = Frames.Changed
type Context = Frames.Context

local Ops = {}

Ops.nudge = {
	-- Its range may run across a looping clip's end (see Seam).
	wraps = true,

	check = function(where: string, operation: any, joints: { [string]: any })
		local chain = if type(operation.part) == "string" then Limb.CHAINS[operation.part] else nil
		if not chain then
			refuse(where, "part must be LeftFoot, RightFoot, LeftHand or RightHand.")
		end
		for _, name in chain :: { string } do
			needJoint(where, name, joints)
		end
		needRange(where, operation, true)
		local offset = operation.offset
		if type(offset) ~= "table" or #offset ~= 3 then
			refuse(where, "offset must be three numbers: studs toward the rig's right, up, and toward its back.")
		end
		for _, value in offset do
			if not isFinite(value) or math.abs(value) > Store.MAX_POSITION then
				refuse(where, `each number of offset must be finite and at most {Store.MAX_POSITION} studs.`)
			end
		end
		if operation.hold ~= nil then
			needOneOf(where, operation.hold, "hold", Store.HOLDS)
		end
		local soft = operation.soft
		if soft ~= nil and (not isFinite(soft) or soft < 0 or soft > 0.5) then
			refuse(where, "soft must be from 0 to 0.5.")
		end
		needBlends(where, operation)
	end,

	apply = function(where: string, clip: Instance, operation: any, context: Context, changed: Changed)
		local chain = Limb.CHAINS[operation.part]
		local joints = context.joints
		if not hasGeometry(joints, chain) then
			refuse(where, "this rig's limb could not be measured, so nothing can be moved on it.")
		end
		local duration = Store.duration(clip)
		if operation.time_to > duration + Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
			refuse(
				where,
				`the clip ends at {milliseconds(duration)} seconds, before time_to.`,
				"Key the clip out to its full length first."
			)
		end
		local from, to = operation.time_from, operation.time_to
		local first = math.max(0, from - (operation.blend_in or 0))
		local last = math.min(duration, to + (operation.blend_out or 0))
		local rate = Store.FRAME_RATE
		local firstFrame = math.ceil(first * rate - FRAME_SLACK)
		local lastFrame = math.floor(last * rate + FRAME_SLACK)
		if lastFrame < firstFrame then
			refuse(where, "the range holds no whole frame; Studio shows a curve clip only at whole frames.")
		end

		-- Everything is worked out from the clip as it is, before anything is written.
		local channels = readChannels(clip)
		local scan = { joints = joints } :: any
		local identity = Roblox.CFrame.new()
		local limb = { joints[chain[1]], joints[chain[2]], joints[chain[3]] }
		local shift = Roblox.Vector3.new(operation.offset[1], operation.offset[2], operation.offset[3])
		-- full: the part is moved without turning, as a point dragged along its trail.
		-- position: only where it is moves, and it turns with the limb.
		local full = (operation.hold or "full") == "full"

		local frames: { { CFrame } } = {}
		local missed, worst, softened, largest = 0, 0, 0, 0
		local missedFrom, missedTo = math.huge, -math.huge
		for frame = firstFrame, lastFrame do
			local time = frame / rate
			local transforms = transformsAt(channels, time)
			local current = { transforms[chain[1]], transforms[chain[2]], transforms[chain[3]] }
			-- How much of the offset applies here: all of it from time_from to time_to,
			-- easing in before and out after.
			local weight = 1
			if time < from - Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
				weight = smoothstep((time - first) / math.max(from - first, 1e-6))
			elseif time > to + Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
				weight = smoothstep((last - time) / math.max(last - to, 1e-6))
			end
			if weight <= 0 then
				table.insert(frames, current)
				continue
			end
			local placed = Pose.place(scan, transforms, identity)
			-- Where the part's own motion has it now, moved by its share of the offset.
			local tip = Roblox.CFrame.new(shift * weight) * placed[chain[3]]
			local solution = Limb.solve({
				parent = placed[Rig.R15_PARENTS[chain[1]]],
				joints = limb,
				current = current,
				pivot = Limb.pivotOf(limb[3], tip),
				tip = if full then tip else nil,
				bend = Limb.BEND[operation.part],
				-- Eased in with the offset, so a limb near full stretch doesn't jump on the
				-- first frame of the blend.
				soft = if operation.soft then operation.soft * weight else nil,
			})
			largest = math.max(largest, shift.Magnitude * weight)
			if not solution.beyond and solution.miss > 0.001 then
				-- Short of the point only because the reach was softened.
				softened = math.max(softened, solution.miss)
			elseif solution.miss > 0.001 then
				missed += 1
				worst = math.max(worst, solution.miss)
				missedFrom = math.min(missedFrom, time)
				missedTo = math.max(missedTo, time)
			end
			table.insert(frames, solution.transforms)
		end

		-- The three joints' rotation keys in the range are replaced by one key a frame.
		for index, joint in chain do
			local turns = {}
			for frame, entry in frames do
				turns[frame] = entry[index]
			end
			writeTurns(clip, joint, channels[joint] or {}, firstFrame, lastFrame, turns, duration, changed, false)
		end
		count(changed, "frames_nudged", #frames)
		changed.largest_nudge_studs = math.max(changed.largest_nudge_studs or 0, rounded(largest, 3))
		if softened > 0 then
			changed.largest_soft_studs = math.max(changed.largest_soft_studs or 0, rounded(softened, 3))
		end
		if missed > 0 then
			count(changed, "frames_out_of_reach", missed)
			changed.largest_miss_studs = math.max(changed.largest_miss_studs or 0, rounded(worst, 3))
			changed.out_of_reach_from = math.min(changed.out_of_reach_from or math.huge, milliseconds(missedFrom))
			changed.out_of_reach_to = math.max(changed.out_of_reach_to or -math.huge, milliseconds(missedTo))
		end
	end,
}

return Ops

--!strict
-- Uart.lua -- 8250/16450 COM1 at 0x3F8-0x3FF.
--
-- The core only models the registers a DOS/Windows serial driver touches. Byte
-- I/O goes through an injected host backend so the module stays environment
-- pure: the Roblox client can wire a terminal, Lune tests use a loopback.

const band, bor, lshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift

const Uart = {}
Uart.__index = Uart

Uart.BASE = 0x3F8
Uart.RX_CAPACITY = 16

export type Backend = {
	writeByte: ((backend: any, value: number) -> ())?,
	readByte: ((backend: any) -> number?)?,
}

export type Uart = {
	backend: Backend?,
	rx: { number },
	overrun: boolean,
	threPending: boolean,
	ier: number,
	lcr: number,
	mcr: number,
	fcr: number,
	divisorLow: number,
	divisorHigh: number,
	scratch: number,
	new: (backend: Backend?) -> Uart,
	reset: (self: Uart) -> (),
	poll: (self: Uart) -> (),
	pushByte: (self: Uart, value: number) -> (),
	rxAvailable: (self: Uart) -> boolean,
	readByte: (self: Uart) -> number?,
	writeByte: (self: Uart, value: number) -> (),
	writeText: (self: Uart, text: string) -> (),
	irqPending: (self: Uart) -> boolean,
	interruptId: (self: Uart) -> number,
	lineStatus: (self: Uart) -> number,
	modemStatus: (self: Uart) -> number,
	in8: (self: Uart, port: number) -> number,
	out8: (self: Uart, port: number, value: number) -> (),
}

function Uart.new(backend: Backend?): Uart
	const self = setmetatable({}, Uart) :: any
	self.backend = backend
	self:reset()
	return self
end

function Uart.reset(self: Uart)
	self.rx = {}
	self.overrun = false
	self.threPending = true -- THR starts empty
	self.ier = 0
	self.lcr = 0x03 -- 8N1
	self.mcr = 0
	self.fcr = 0
	self.divisorLow = 12 -- 9600 with a 1.8432 MHz clock
	self.divisorHigh = 0
	self.scratch = 0
end

-- Pull one byte from the host backend. Called from the IRQ pump and on a
-- register read so polled and interrupt-driven guests both see input.
function Uart.poll(self: Uart)
	if #self.rx >= Uart.RX_CAPACITY then
		return
	end
	const backend = self.backend
	if not backend or not backend.readByte then
		return
	end
	const value = backend.readByte(backend)
	if value ~= nil then
		self.rx[#self.rx + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
	end
end

function Uart.pushByte(self: Uart, value: number)
	self:poll()
	if #self.rx >= Uart.RX_CAPACITY then
		self.overrun = true
		return
	end
	self.rx[#self.rx + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
end

function Uart.rxAvailable(self: Uart): boolean
	self:poll()
	return #self.rx > 0
end

function Uart.readByte(self: Uart): number?
	self:poll()
	if #self.rx == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	return table.remove(self.rx, 1)
end

-- A real 8250 in loopback returns TX to RX without touching the line. The
-- backend is only called for normal (non-loopback) transmission.
function Uart.writeByte(self: Uart, value: number)
	const byte = band(value, 0xFF)
	if band(self.mcr, 0x10) ~= 0 then
		self:pushByte(byte)
	else
		const backend = self.backend
		if backend and backend.writeByte then
			backend.writeByte(backend, byte)
		end
	end
	self.threPending = true
end

function Uart.writeText(self: Uart, text: string)
	for index = 1, #text do
		self:writeByte(string.byte(text, index) :: number)
	end
end

-- OUT2 (MCR bit 3) gates the card's IRQ line on a real PC.
function Uart.irqPending(self: Uart): boolean
	if band(self.mcr, 0x08) == 0 then
		return false
	end
	if band(self.ier, 0x01) ~= 0 then
		self:poll()
		if #self.rx > 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	if band(self.ier, 0x02) ~= 0 and self.threPending then
		return true
	end
	return false
end

-- IIR: bit 0 = 0 means pending; bits 3-1 are the highest-priority source.
-- Reading IIR acknowledges a pending THRE interrupt.
function Uart.interruptId(self: Uart): number
	const fifo = if band(self.fcr, 0x01) ~= 0 then 0xC0 else 0
	const value = (function(): number
		if band(self.ier, 0x01) ~= 0 then
			self:poll()
			if #self.rx > 0 then
				return bor(fifo, 0x04) -- received data available
			end
		end
		if band(self.ier, 0x02) ~= 0 and self.threPending then
			return bor(fifo, 0x02) -- transmitter holding register empty
		end
		return 0x01
	end)()
	if band(value, 0x0E) == 0x02 then
		self.threPending = false
	end
	return value
end

function Uart.lineStatus(self: Uart): number
	self:poll()
	local status = 0x60 -- THRE and TEMT
	if #self.rx > 0 then
		status = bor(status, 0x01)
	end
	if self.overrun then
		status = bor(status, 0x02)
	end
	return status
end

function Uart.modemStatus(self: Uart): number
	if band(self.mcr, 0x10) ~= 0 then
		-- Loopback: CTS/DSR/RI/DCD mirror RTS/DTR/OUT1/OUT2.
		return lshift(band(self.mcr, 0x0F), 4)
	end
	return 0xB0 -- DCD, DSR and CTS asserted; no delta bits
end

function Uart.in8(self: Uart, port: number): number
	const offset = band(port - Uart.BASE, 0xFF)
	if offset == 0 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			return self.divisorLow
		end
		return self:readByte() or 0
	elseif offset == 1 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			return self.divisorHigh
		end
		return self.ier
	elseif offset == 2 then
		return self:interruptId()
	elseif offset == 3 then
		return self.lcr
	elseif offset == 4 then
		return self.mcr
	elseif offset == 5 then
		const status = self:lineStatus()
		self.overrun = false
		return status
	elseif offset == 6 then
		return self:modemStatus()
	elseif offset == 7 then
		return self.scratch
	end
	return 0
end

function Uart.out8(self: Uart, port: number, value: number)
	const byte = band(value, 0xFF)
	const offset = band(port - Uart.BASE, 0xFF)
	if offset == 0 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			self.divisorLow = byte
		else
			self:writeByte(byte) -- THR
		end
	elseif offset == 1 then
		if band(self.lcr, 0x80) ~= 0 then
			self.divisorHigh = byte
		else
			self.ier = band(byte, 0x0F)
		end
	elseif offset == 2 then
		self.fcr = byte
		if band(byte, 0x02) ~= 0 then -- clear receive FIFO
			self.rx = {}
			self.overrun = false
		end
	elseif offset == 3 then
		self.lcr = byte
	elseif offset == 4 then
		self.mcr = byte
	elseif offset == 7 then
		self.scratch = byte
	end
end

-- In-memory loopback backend: transmitted bytes come back as received bytes.
-- Tests use this, and it is a useful default for a host with no terminal.
function Uart.loopbackBackend(): Backend
	const queue: { number } = {}
	return {
		writeByte = function(_backend: any, value: number)
			queue[#queue + 1] = band(value, 0xFF)
		end,
		readByte = function(_backend: any): number?
			return table.remove(queue, 1)
		end,
	}
end

return Uart

  0xba, 0x78, 0x25, 0x2e, 0x1c, 0xa6, 0xb4, 0xc6, 0xe8, 0xdd, 0x74, 0x1f, 0x4b, 0xbd, 0x8b, 0x8a,
  0x70, 0x3e, 0xb5, 0x66, 0x48, 0x03, 0xf6, 0x0e, 0x61, 0x35, 0x57, 0xb9, 0x86, 0xc1, 0x1d, 0x9e,
  0xe1, 0xf8, 0x98, 0x11, 0x69, 0xd9, 0x8e, 0x94, 0x9b, 0x1e, 0x87, 0xe9, 0xce, 0x55, 0x28, 0xdf,

assert(#SBOX == 256, "S-box must have 256 entries")

-- Derive the four T-tables at startup.
-- Te0[x] packs (2*S, S, S, 3*S) MSB-first; Te1..Te3 are byte rotations.
local Te0 = table.create(256, 0)
local Te1 = table.create(256, 0)
local Te2 = table.create(256, 0)
local Te3 = table.create(256, 0)

local function xtime(x) -- GF(2^8) multiply by 2, modulo x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1
  x = x * 2
  if x >= 256 then x = bxor(x - 256, 0x1b) end
  return x
end

for i = 0, 255 do
  local s = SBOX[i + 1]
  local s2 = xtime(s)
  local s3 = bxor(s2, s)
  local w = bor(lshift(s2, 24), lshift(s, 16), lshift(s, 8), s3)
  Te0[i + 1] = w
  Te1[i + 1] = rrotate(w, 8)  -- (3S, 2S, S, S)
  Te2[i + 1] = rrotate(w, 16) -- (S, 3S, 2S, S)
  Te3[i + 1] = rrotate(w, 24) -- (S, S, 3S, 2S)
end

-- Key schedule: 16-byte key (as 4 big-endian words) -> 44 round-key words.
local RCON = { 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x1b, 0x36 }

local function expandKey(k0, k1, k2, k3)
  local w = table.create(44, 0)
  w[1], w[2], w[3], w[4] = k0, k1, k2, k3
  for i = 5, 44 do
    local t = w[i - 1]
    if (i - 1) % 4 == 0 then
      -- RotWord then SubWord then XOR rcon into the top byte
      t = lrotate(t, 8)
      t = bor(
        lshift(SBOX[rshift(t, 24) + 1], 24),
        lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(t, 16), 255) + 1], 16),
        lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(t, 8), 255) + 1], 8),
        SBOX[band(t, 255) + 1])
      t = bxor(t, lshift(RCON[(i - 1) / 4], 24))
    end
    w[i] = bxor(w[i - 4], t)
  end
  return w
end

-- Encrypt one block. State lives entirely in locals s0..s3 / u0..u3.
-- rk is the flat 44-word round-key array.
local function encryptBlock(rk, s0, s1, s2, s3)
  -- initial AddRoundKey
  s0 = bxor(s0, rk[1])
  s1 = bxor(s1, rk[2])
  s2 = bxor(s2, rk[3])
  s3 = bxor(s3, rk[4])

  -- 9 full rounds via T-table lookups
  local base = 4
  for _ = 1, 9 do
    local u0 = bxor(
      Te0[rshift(s0, 24) + 1],
      Te1[band(rshift(s1, 16), 255) + 1],
      Te2[band(rshift(s2, 8), 255) + 1],
      Te3[band(s3, 255) + 1], rk[base + 1])
    local u1 = bxor(
      Te0[rshift(s1, 24) + 1],
      Te1[band(rshift(s2, 16), 255) + 1],
      Te2[band(rshift(s3, 8), 255) + 1],
      Te3[band(s0, 255) + 1], rk[base + 2])
    local u2 = bxor(
      Te0[rshift(s2, 24) + 1],
      Te1[band(rshift(s3, 16), 255) + 1],
      Te2[band(rshift(s0, 8), 255) + 1],
      Te3[band(s1, 255) + 1], rk[base + 3])
    local u3 = bxor(
      Te0[rshift(s3, 24) + 1],
      Te1[band(rshift(s0, 16), 255) + 1],
      Te2[band(rshift(s1, 8), 255) + 1],
      Te3[band(s2, 255) + 1], rk[base + 4])
    s0, s1, s2, s3 = u0, u1, u2, u3
    base = base + 4
  end

  -- final round: SubBytes + ShiftRows + AddRoundKey (no MixColumns)
  local t0 = bxor(bor(
    lshift(SBOX[rshift(s0, 24) + 1], 24),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s1, 16), 255) + 1], 16),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s2, 8), 255) + 1], 8),
    SBOX[band(s3, 255) + 1]), rk[41])
  local t1 = bxor(bor(
    lshift(SBOX[rshift(s1, 24) + 1], 24),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s2, 16), 255) + 1], 16),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s3, 8), 255) + 1], 8),
    SBOX[band(s0, 255) + 1]), rk[42])
  local t2 = bxor(bor(
    lshift(SBOX[rshift(s2, 24) + 1], 24),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s3, 16), 255) + 1], 16),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s0, 8), 255) + 1], 8),
    SBOX[band(s1, 255) + 1]), rk[43])
  local t3 = bxor(bor(
    lshift(SBOX[rshift(s3, 24) + 1], 24),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s0, 16), 255) + 1], 16),
    lshift(SBOX[band(rshift(s1, 8), 255) + 1], 8),
    SBOX[band(s2, 255) + 1]), rk[44])

  return t0, t1, t2, t3
end

-- Correctness check: FIPS-197 Appendix C.1 single-block ECB vector.
-- key       000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f
-- plaintext 00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff
-- cipher    69c4e0d86a7b0430d8cdb78070b4c55a
do
  local rk = expandKey(0x00010203, 0x04050607, 0x08090a0b, 0x0c0d0e0f)
  local c0, c1, c2, c3 = encryptBlock(rk,
    0x00112233, 0x44556677, 0x8899aabb, 0xccddeeff)
  assert(c0 == 0x69c4e0d8 and c1 == 0x6a7b0430 and
         c2 == 0xd8cdb780 and c3 == 0x70b4c55a,
    string.format("FIPS-197 vector FAILED: got %08x %08x %08x %08x",
      c0, c1, c2, c3))
end

-- Bulk workload: CTR-mode encrypt BULK_KB of seeded plaintext.
-- Counter block = fixed 96-bit nonce || 32-bit block counter.
local BLOCKS = BULK_KB * 64 -- 16 bytes per block
local NONCE0, NONCE1, NONCE2 = 0xdeadbeef, 0x01234567, 0x89abcdef
local roundKeys = expandKey(0x2b7e1516, 0x28aed2a6, 0xabf71588, 0x09cf4f3c)

local t0 = os.clock()

local seed = PRNG_SEED
local checksum = 0x811c9dc5
for ctr = 1, BLOCKS do
  -- keystream block: encrypt nonce||counter
  local k0, k1, k2, k3 = encryptBlock(roundKeys, NONCE0, NONCE1, NONCE2, ctr)

  -- four words of seeded plaintext (Park-Miller, exact in doubles)
  seed = seed * 48271 % 2147483647
  local p0 = seed
  seed = seed * 48271 % 2147483647
  local p1 = seed
  seed = seed * 48271 % 2147483647
  local p2 = seed
  seed = seed * 48271 % 2147483647
  local p3 = seed

  -- XOR keystream into plaintext, fold ciphertext into rotate-XOR checksum
  checksum = bxor(lrotate(checksum, 5), bxor(k0, p0))
  checksum = bxor(lrotate(checksum, 5), bxor(k1, p1))
  checksum = bxor(lrotate(checksum, 5), bxor(k2, p2))
  checksum = bxor(lrotate(checksum, 5), bxor(k3, p3))
end

local elapsed = os.clock() - t0

local EXPECTED_CHECKSUM = 0xe8fe84b4 -- discovered once for BULK_KB=192, baked in
assert(checksum == EXPECTED_CHECKSUM,
  string.format("checksum mismatch: got %08x, want %08x",
    checksum, EXPECTED_CHECKSUM))

print(string.format("aes128 checksum: %s", string.format("%08x", checksum)))
print("main work time", elapsed * 1000)
print("entire script time", (os.clock() - __BENCH_T0__) * 1000)

-- UIListLayout's flex and wrapping and UIFlexItem: where they put three
-- children and what the list reports, in a fixed 400 x 300 box.
--! client
local player = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- Rounded, and + 0 turns -0 (float noise) into 0.
local function v(p)
	return string.format("%g,%g", math.round(p.X * 100) / 100 + 0, math.round(p.Y * 100) / 100 + 0)
end
local box = Instance.new("Frame")
box.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(400, 300)
box.Parent = screen
local list = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
list.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
list.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
list.Parent = box
local items = {}
for i, w in { 50, 100, 30 } do
	local f = Instance.new("Frame")
	f.Name = "F" .. i
	f.LayoutOrder = i
	f.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(w, 20 + i * 10)
	f.Parent = box
	items[i] = f
end
local function dump(tag)
	local out = {}
	for _, f in items do
		table.insert(out, f.Name .. "@" .. v(f.AbsolutePosition - box.AbsolutePosition) .. "/" .. v(f.AbsoluteSize))
	end
	log(tag, table.concat(out, " "), "content", v(list.AbsoluteContentSize))
end
local function sizes(a, b, c)
	items[1].Size = UDim2.fromOffset(a, 30)
	items[2].Size = UDim2.fromOffset(b, 40)
	items[3].Size = UDim2.fromOffset(c, 50)
end

for _, name in { "Fill", "SpaceAround", "SpaceBetween", "SpaceEvenly" } do
	list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment[name]
	dump("along " .. name)
end
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
for _, name in { "Fill", "SpaceAround", "SpaceBetween" } do
	list.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment[name]
	dump("across " .. name)
end
list.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.Start
dump("across Fill, line Start")
list.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 10)
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.Fill
dump("Fill, padded")
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 0)
for _, name in { "Center", "End", "Stretch" } do
	list.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment[name]
	dump("line " .. name)
end
list.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.Center
list.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Bottom
dump("line Center, bottom")
list.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.Automatic
list.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Top

local item = Instance.new("UIFlexItem")
item.Parent = items[2]
for _, name in { "Grow", "Shrink", "Fill" } do
	item.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode[name]
	dump("F2 " .. name)
end
item.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.End
dump("F2 Fill, line End")
item.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.Automatic
item.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode.Custom
item.GrowRatio = 2
local other = Instance.new("UIFlexItem")
other.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode.Custom
other.GrowRatio = 1
other.Parent = items[1]
dump("grow 1 and 2")
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.Fill
dump("grow 1 and 2, list Fill")
other.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode.None
dump("F1 None, list Fill")
other:Destroy()
item:Destroy()

sizes(200, 300, 30)
dump("too long, list Fill")
local limit = Instance.new("UISizeConstraint")
limit.MinSize = Vector2.new(190, 0)
limit.Parent = items[1]
dump("too long, F1 at least 190")
limit:Destroy()
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
item = Instance.new("UIFlexItem")
item.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode.Custom
item.ShrinkRatio = 3
item.Parent = items[2]
other = Instance.new("UIFlexItem")
other.FlexMode = Enum.UIFlexMode.Shrink
other.Parent = items[1]
dump("too long, shrink 1 and 3")
item:Destroy()
other:Destroy()
dump("too long, no flex")

sizes(150, 200, 100)
list.Wraps = true
list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 10)
dump("wraps, padded")
list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 0)
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.SpaceBetween
dump("wraps, SpaceBetween")
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.Fill
dump("wraps, Fill")
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
for _, name in { "Fill", "SpaceBetween", "SpaceEvenly" } do
	list.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment[name]
	dump("wraps, across " .. name)
end
list.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.None
list.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Bottom
list.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
dump("wraps, bottom, centered")
list.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Vertical
list.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Top
list.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Left
list.Wraps = false
list.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.SpaceBetween
list.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.Fill
dump("vertical, SpaceBetween, across Fill")

screen:Destroy()

--!strict
-- Follow-through: a chain trailing the body's motion through a damped spring.

local Frames = require("./Frames")
local Body = require("./Body")
local Need = require("./Need")
local Pose = require("../../Rigs/Pose")
local Rig = require("../../Rigs/Rig")
local Roblox = require("../../Core/Roblox")
local Store = require("./Store")
local Write = require("./Write")

local count = Frames.count
local hasGeometry = Body.hasGeometry
local isFinite = Need.isFinite
local near = Frames.near
local needBlends = Need.needBlends
local needJoints = Need.needJoints
local needRange = Need.needRange
local readChannels = Frames.readChannels
local refuse = Need.refuse
local spanOf = Frames.spanOf
local transformsAt = Frames.transformsAt
local writeTurns = Write.writeTurns

type Changed = Frames.Changed
type Context = Frames.Context

local Ops = {}

Ops.overlap = {
	-- Its range may run across a looping clip's end (see Seam).
	wraps = true,

	check = function(where: string, operation: any, joints: { [string]: any })
		if type(operation.joints) ~= "table" or #operation.joints == 0 then
			refuse(where, "joints must name at least one joint.")
		end
		needJoints(where, operation.joints, joints)
		needRange(where, operation, true)
		local lag = operation.lag
		if lag ~= nil and (not isFinite(lag) or lag < Store.MIN_LAG or lag > Store.MAX_LAG) then
			refuse(where, `lag must be from {Store.MIN_LAG} to {Store.MAX_LAG} seconds.`)
		end
		local bounce = operation.bounce
		if bounce ~= nil and (not isFinite(bounce) or bounce < 0 or bounce > Store.MAX_BOUNCE) then
			refuse(where, `bounce must be from 0 to {Store.MAX_BOUNCE}.`)
		end
		local weight = operation.weight
		if weight ~= nil and (not isFinite(weight) or weight < 0 or weight > 1) then
			refuse(where, "weight must be from 0 to 1.")
		end
		needBlends(where, operation)
	end,

	apply = function(where: string, clip: Instance, operation: any, context: Context, changed: Changed)
		local joints = context.joints
		if not hasGeometry(joints, Rig.R15_ORDER) then
			refuse(where, "this rig's joints could not be measured, so nothing can trail on it.")
		end
		local span = spanOf(where, clip, operation)
		local channels = readChannels(clip)
		local scan = { joints = joints } :: any
		local identity = Roblox.CFrame.new()
		local function turnOf(cframe: CFrame): CFrame
			return cframe - cframe.Position
		end
		-- From the body outward, so that each joint trails a parent that already trails.
		local named: { [string]: boolean } = {}
		for _, name in operation.joints do
			named[name] = true
		end
		local chain: { string } = {}
		for _, name in Rig.R15_ORDER do
			if named[name] then
				table.insert(chain, name)
			end
		end
		local rests: { [string]: { CFrame } } = {}
		for _, name in chain do
			local c0, c1 = Rig.rest(joints[name])
			rests[name] = { turnOf(c0), turnOf(c1) }
		end

		-- A damped spring on each part's turn in the room, pulled toward where the clip
		-- would put it on its (trailing) parent: it lags into a move and, with bounce, swings
		-- past where it stops before settling.
		-- The lag is shared along the chain, so its end trails by about that much: springs
		-- one after another each add their own.
		local lag = operation.lag or 0.1
		local stiffness = #chain / lag
		local damping = 1 - (operation.bounce or 0.3)
		local weight = operation.weight or 1
		local rate = Store.FRAME_RATE
		local steps = 8
		local dt = 1 / rate / steps
		local duration = Store.duration(clip)
		local whole = near(operation.time_from, 0) and near(operation.time_to, duration)
		local looping = (clip :: any).Loop == true and whole
		local frameCount = span.last - span.first + 1

		local animated: { { [string]: CFrame } } = {}
		local frames: { { [string]: CFrame } } = {}
		for index = 1, frameCount do
			local transforms = transformsAt(channels, (span.first + index - 1) / rate)
			animated[index] = transforms
			frames[index] = Pose.place(scan, transforms, identity)
		end
		local state: { [string]: { turn: CFrame, spin: Vector3 } } = {}
		local turns: { [string]: { CFrame } } = {}
		for _, name in chain do
			turns[name] = {}
		end
		-- A looping clip is run round three times and the last kept, by when the springs
		-- have settled into the cycle, so the motion comes back round to where it began.
		local passes = if looping then 3 else 1
		for pass = 1, passes do
			-- In a loop the last frame is the first one again, so the round before the one
			-- kept stops short of it.
			local last = if pass < passes then frameCount - 1 else frameCount
			for index = 1, last do
				local time = (span.first + index - 1) / rate
				local placed = frames[index]
				local blend = weight * span.weight(time)
				local final: { [string]: CFrame } = {}
				for _, name in chain do
					local parentName = Rig.R15_PARENTS[name]
					local parent = final[parentName] or turnOf(placed[parentName] or identity)
					local c0, c1 = rests[name][1], rests[name][2]
					local own = turnOf(animated[index][name])
					-- Where the clip would put the part on its parent as it now is.
					local goal = parent * c0 * own * c1:Inverse()
					local spring = state[name]
					if not spring then
						spring = { turn = goal, spin = Roblox.Vector3.new() }
						state[name] = spring
					end
					for _ = 1, steps do
						local axis, angle = (goal * spring.turn:Inverse()):ToAxisAngle()
						local pull = if angle > 1e-9 then axis.Unit * angle else Roblox.Vector3.new()
						spring.spin += (pull * stiffness * stiffness - spring.spin * 2 * damping * stiffness) * dt
						local step = spring.spin * dt
						if step.Magnitude > 1e-12 then
							spring.turn = Roblox.CFrame.fromAxisAngle(step.Unit, step.Magnitude) * spring.turn
						end
					end
					local result = goal:Lerp(spring.turn, blend)
					final[name] = result
					if pass == passes then
						turns[name][index] = Roblox.CFrame.new(animated[index][name].Position)
							* (c0:Inverse() * parent:Inverse() * result * c1)
					end
				end
			end
		end
		for _, name in chain do
			writeTurns(clip, name, channels[name] or {}, span.first, span.last, turns[name], duration, changed, true)
		end
		count(changed, "frames_with_overlap", frameCount)
	end,
}

return Ops

--!strict
-- Vga.lua -- environment-pure VGA device model for RVPC.
--
-- The device owns the A0000..AFFFF aperture rather than Memory: a real VGA has
-- four 64 KiB planes behind one 64 KiB window, so the linear 1 MiB buffer
-- cannot represent it. Machine must route A0000..AFFFF accesses here and call
-- in8/out8 for 0x3C0..0x3DA. Unknown ports and registers latch instead of
-- faulting; VGA.DRV probes several of them during mode set.
--
-- Implemented: mode 12h (640x480x16 planar), mode 13h (320x200x256 linear),
-- text mode 3 fallback, write modes 0/1/2/3, read modes 0/1, set/reset,
-- enable set/reset, data rotate, logical operations, read map select, colour
-- compare/don't-care, bit mask, map mask, odd/even host addressing, CRTC
-- start/offset, attribute-controller palette selection (including AR14 colour
-- select), and DAC writes. Text mode 3 reads B8000 directly through mem and
-- does not use odd/even plane addressing. Mode 13h collapses chain-4 address
-- decode to a linear 64 KiB buffer; its write modes and bit mask are not
-- applied.
--
-- Mode 12h reads and writes decode the four planes at the same byte address.
-- Latches load on every aperture read. Write mode 3 always uses GC0 set/reset
-- (GC1 is ignored) and preserves bit-mask-zero bits from the latches, matching
-- VGA hardware. Odd/even host addressing is implemented for CPU reads/writes;
-- the CGA/EGA shift-register display formats are not. The CRTC 0x22 alias
-- exposes the four latches, as on real VGA hardware.
--
-- A guest VGA BIOS programs the controllers through I/O ports instead of
-- calling setMode, so syncLegacyMode infers text/planar/linear and the visible
-- geometry from GC6/AR10 and the CRTC registers. INT 10h AX=0012 therefore
-- reaches the planar renderer on its own.
--
-- Text mode 3 also models CRTC cursor start/end/location, the cursor
-- enable/disable bit, the text attribute blink phase, and the hardware cursor
-- in snapshots. Not implemented: sync timing, interlace/double-scan timing,
-- CGA/EGA 2bpp shift-register output, chain-2 memory, horizontal pel/byte
-- panning, split-screen line compare, the GC6 memory-map windows at
-- B0000/B8000, and the 256 KiB VGA memory map beyond the first 64 KiB.

const FONT_BYTES = table.concat(FONT_HEX, "")

local function decodeFont(): { [number]: { number } }
	local glyphs: { [number]: { number } } = {}
	for code = 32, 126 do
		const rows = table.create(8, 0) :: { number }
		const base = (code - 32) * 16 + 1
		for row = 0, 7 do
			const first = base + row * 2
			rows[row] = tonumber(string.sub(FONT_BYTES, first, first + 1), 16) or 0
		end
		glyphs[code] = rows
	end
	return glyphs
end

const FONT = decodeFont()

local function dac6To8(value: number): number
	const component = band(value, 0x3F)
	return bor(lshift(component, 2), rshift(component, 4))
end

local function rgbaWord(r: number, g: number, b: number): number
	return bor(bor(bor(r, lshift(g, 8)), lshift(b, 16)), 0xFF000000)
end

local function apertureOffset(addr: number): number
	if addr >= APERTURE_BASE then
		return band(addr - APERTURE_BASE, 0xFFFF)
	end
	return band(addr, 0xFFFF)
end

local function rotateRight(value: number, count: number): number
	if count == 0 then
		return band(value, 0xFF)
	end
	return band(bor(rshift(value, count), lshift(value, 8 - count)), 0xFF)
end

local function applyDataFunction(data: number, latch: number, fn: number): number
	if fn == 1 then
		return band(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 2 then
		return bor(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 3 then
		return bxor(data, latch)
	end
	return data
end

-- Cheap routing predicate for a Memory/CPU aperture hook. The low VGA aperture
-- is still reported for compatibility; the high LFB is the SVGA addition.
function Vga.containsAddress(addr: number): boolean
	if addr >= VBE_FRAMEBUFFER_BASE and addr < VBE_FRAMEBUFFER_END then
		return true
	end
	const physical = band(addr, 0xFFFFF)
	return physical >= APERTURE_BASE and physical < APERTURE_BASE + APERTURE_SIZE
end
