--!strict
-- Holding a hand or foot in place, on a moving floor, against another part, or rolling.

local Frames = require("./Frames")
local Body = require("./Body")
local Limb = require("../../Rigs/Limb")
local Need = require("./Need")
local Pose = require("../../Rigs/Pose")
local Rig = require("../../Rigs/Rig")
local Roblox = require("../../Core/Roblox")
local Store = require("./Store")
local Write = require("./Write")

local count = Frames.count
local floorOf = Body.floorOf
local FRAME_SLACK = Frames.FRAME_SLACK
local hasGeometry = Body.hasGeometry
local isFinite = Need.isFinite
local milliseconds = Need.milliseconds
local needBlends = Need.needBlends
local needJoint = Need.needJoint
local needOneOf = Need.needOneOf
local needRange = Need.needRange
local needTime = Need.needTime
local needVector = Need.needVector
local readChannels = Frames.readChannels
local refuse = Need.refuse
local rounded = Need.rounded
local smoothstep = Frames.smoothstep
local transformsAt = Frames.transformsAt
local writeFrames = Write.writeFrames
local writeTurns = Write.writeTurns

type Changed = Frames.Changed
type Context = Frames.Context

local Ops = {}

Ops.pin = {
	-- Its range may run across a looping clip's end (see Seam).
	wraps = true,

	check = function(where: string, operation: any, joints: { [string]: any })
		local chain = if type(operation.part) == "string" then Limb.CHAINS[operation.part] else nil
		if not chain then
			refuse(where, "part must be LeftFoot, RightFoot, LeftHand or RightHand.")
		end
		for _, name in chain :: { string } do
			needJoint(where, name, joints)
		end
		needRange(where, operation, true)
		if operation.at ~= nil then
			needTime(where, operation.at, "at")
		end
		needVector(where, operation.position, "position", Store.MAX_POSITION)
		needVector(where, operation.pole, "pole", Store.MAX_POSITION)
		if operation.pivot ~= nil then
			needOneOf(where, operation.pivot, "pivot", Store.PIVOTS)
			if operation.pivot ~= "ankle" then
				if operation.part ~= "LeftFoot" and operation.part ~= "RightFoot" then
					refuse(where, "a toe or heel pivot is for a foot.")
				end
				if operation.hold == "position" then
					refuse(where, "a toe or heel pivot sets how the foot turns; hold position holds the ankle instead.")
				end
			end
		end
		if operation.travel ~= "match" then
			needVector(where, operation.travel, "travel", 100)
		end
		if operation.fit_hips ~= nil and type(operation.fit_hips) ~= "boolean" then
			refuse(where, "fit_hips must be true or false.")
		end
		if operation.fit_hips and operation.relative_to ~= nil then
			refuse(where, "fit_hips moves the hips, which a part held relative_to would move with.")
		end
		if operation.keep ~= nil then
			if not operation.fit_hips then
				refuse(where, "keep is for fit_hips: the limbs held still while the hips move.")
			end
			if type(operation.keep) ~= "table" then
				refuse(where, "keep must list hands or feet.")
			end
			for _, name in operation.keep do
				if type(name) ~= "string" or not Limb.CHAINS[name] or name == operation.part then
					refuse(where, "keep must list other hands or feet: LeftFoot, RightFoot, LeftHand, RightHand.")
				end
				for _, joint in Limb.CHAINS[name] do
					needJoint(where, joint, joints)
				end
			end
		end
		if operation.roll ~= nil then
			if operation.pivot ~= "toe" and operation.pivot ~= "heel" then
				refuse(where, "roll is for a toe or heel pivot.")
			end
			if type(operation.roll) ~= "table" or #operation.roll ~= 2 then
				refuse(where, "roll must be two angles in degrees: at time_from and at time_to.")
			end
			for _, angle in operation.roll do
				if not isFinite(angle) or angle < 0 or angle > 90 then
					refuse(where, "each roll angle must be from 0 to 90 degrees.")
				end
			end
		end
		local soft = operation.soft
		if soft ~= nil and (not isFinite(soft) or soft < 0 or soft > 0.5) then
			refuse(where, "soft must be from 0 to 0.5.")
		end
		if operation.on_floor ~= nil and type(operation.on_floor) ~= "boolean" then
			refuse(where, "on_floor must be true or false.")
		end
		if operation.on_floor and operation.relative_to ~= nil then
			refuse(where, "on_floor holds the part on the floor, so it cannot also be relative_to another part.")
		end
		if operation.relative_to ~= nil then
			needJoint(where, operation.relative_to, joints)
			if table.find(chain :: { string }, operation.relative_to) then
				refuse(where, `relative_to cannot be a part of the limb being pinned.`)
			end
		end
		if operation.hold ~= nil then
			needOneOf(where, operation.hold, "hold", Store.HOLDS)
		end
		needBlends(where, operation)
	end,

	apply = function(where: string, clip: Instance, operation: any, context: Context, changed: Changed)
		local chain = Limb.CHAINS[operation.part]
		local joints = context.joints
		if not hasGeometry(joints, chain) then
			refuse(where, "this rig's limb could not be measured, so nothing can be pinned on it.")
		end
		local duration = Store.duration(clip)
		if operation.time_to > duration + Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
			refuse(
				where,
				`the clip ends at {milliseconds(duration)} seconds, before time_to.`,
				"Key the clip out to its full length first."
			)
		end
		local from, to = operation.time_from, operation.time_to
		local first = math.max(0, from - (operation.blend_in or 0))
		local last = math.min(duration, to + (operation.blend_out or 0))
		local rate = Store.FRAME_RATE
		local firstFrame = math.ceil(first * rate - FRAME_SLACK)
		local lastFrame = math.floor(last * rate + FRAME_SLACK)
		if lastFrame < firstFrame then
			refuse(where, "the range holds no whole frame; Studio shows a curve clip only at whole frames.")
		end

		-- Everything is worked out from the clip as it is, before anything is written.
		local channels = readChannels(clip)
		local scan = { joints = joints } :: any
		local identity = Roblox.CFrame.new()
		local limb = { joints[chain[1]], joints[chain[2]], joints[chain[3]] }
		-- The part the target moves with, if any: the target is kept in its frame, so a
		-- hand held to the chest stays on the chest as the body bends.
		local anchorName = operation.relative_to
		local function anchorOf(placed: { [string]: CFrame }): CFrame
			return if anchorName then placed[anchorName] else identity
		end
		local reference = Pose.place(scan, transformsAt(channels, operation.at or from), identity)
		-- The target, in the anchor's frame.
		local tipLocal = anchorOf(reference):Inverse() * reference[chain[3]]
		if operation.position then
			local p = operation.position
			tipLocal = Roblox.CFrame.new(p[1], p[2], p[3]) * (tipLocal - tipLocal.Position)
		end
		if operation.on_floor then
			-- Where it is, but set flat, turned only about the vertical, with its underside
			-- on the floor.
			local here = tipLocal.Position
			local look = tipLocal.LookVector
			local heading = Roblox.Vector3.new(look.X, 0, look.Z)
			if heading.Magnitude < 1e-6 then
				heading = Roblox.Vector3.new(0, 0, -1)
			end
			local size = joints[chain[3]].part1.Size
			local standing = Roblox.Vector3.new(here.X, floorOf(joints) + size.Y / 2, here.Z)
			tipLocal = Roblox.CFrame.lookAt(standing, standing + heading.Unit)
		end
		-- With a toe or heel pivot, that point of the foot is what stays put, and the foot
		-- turns about it by the roll asked for: its other end lifted off the floor by an
		-- angle that eases from the first given to the second across the range.
		local rolling = operation.pivot == "toe" or operation.pivot == "heel"
		local offset = Roblox.Vector3.new()
		local pointLocal = Roblox.Vector3.new()
		local heldTurn = identity
		if rolling then
			local size = joints[chain[3]].part1.Size
			-- A rig faces along its own negative Z: the toe is the front of the sole.
			offset = Roblox.Vector3.new(0, -size.Y / 2, if operation.pivot == "toe" then -size.Z / 2 else size.Z / 2)
			local atFoot = anchorOf(reference):Inverse() * reference[chain[3]]
			pointLocal = atFoot:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
			heldTurn = atFoot - atFoot.Position
			if operation.position then
				local p = operation.position
				pointLocal = Roblox.Vector3.new(p[1], p[2], p[3])
			end
			if operation.on_floor then
				pointLocal = Roblox.Vector3.new(pointLocal.X, floorOf(joints), pointLocal.Z)
				-- Flat on the floor before it rolls: turned only about the vertical.
				local look = heldTurn.LookVector
				local heading = Roblox.Vector3.new(look.X, 0, look.Z)
				if heading.Magnitude < 1e-6 then
					heading = Roblox.Vector3.new(0, 0, -1)
				end
				heldTurn = Roblox.CFrame.lookAt(Roblox.Vector3.new(), heading.Unit)
			end
		end
		local rollFrom = math.rad(if operation.roll then operation.roll[1] else 0)
		local rollTo = math.rad(if operation.roll then operation.roll[2] else 0)
		-- Lifting the heel turns the foot one way about its own X axis, lifting the toes the
		-- other.
		local lift = if operation.pivot == "toe" then -1 else 1
		if rolling and not operation.on_floor then
			-- The foot is taken to be rolled already by the first angle where it is held,
			-- as after another roll; its facing flat is that, rolled back.
			heldTurn = heldTurn * Roblox.CFrame.Angles(-lift * rollFrom, 0, 0)
		end
		local full = rolling or (operation.hold or "full") == "full"
		local poleLocal = if operation.pole
			then Roblox.Vector3.new(operation.pole[1], operation.pole[2], operation.pole[3])
			else nil

		-- The floor's speed: as given, or with "match" the clip's own motion of the held
		-- point from the start of the range to its end, before this pin changes it.
		local travel: Vector3? = nil
		if operation.travel == "match" then
			local function heldPoint(time: number): Vector3
				local placed = Pose.place(scan, transformsAt(channels, time), identity)
				local part = anchorOf(placed):Inverse() * placed[chain[3]]
				return if rolling then part:PointToWorldSpace(offset) else part.Position
			end
			local velocity = (heldPoint(to) - heldPoint(from)) / math.max(to - from, 1e-6)
			if operation.on_floor then
				velocity = Roblox.Vector3.new(velocity.X, 0, velocity.Z)
			end
			travel = velocity
			changed.travel_x = rounded(velocity.X, 3)
			changed.travel_y = rounded(velocity.Y, 3)
			changed.travel_z = rounded(velocity.Z, 3)
		elseif operation.travel then
			travel = Roblox.Vector3.new(operation.travel[1], operation.travel[2], operation.travel[3])
		end

		-- For fit_hips: which way is up for the hips' position, the hips' drop at each
		-- frame, and the limbs to keep where they are.
		local rootC0 = Rig.rest(joints.LowerTorso)
		local hipsUp = rootC0:VectorToObjectSpace(Roblox.Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
		local drops: { number } = {}
		local hipsDropped, deepest = 0, 0
		local keepChains: { { part: string, chain: { string }, limb: { any }, turns: { [string]: { CFrame } } } } = {}
		for _, name in operation.keep or {} do
			local other = Limb.CHAINS[name]
			table.insert(keepChains, {
				part = name,
				chain = other,
				limb = { joints[other[1]], joints[other[2]], joints[other[3]] },
				turns = { [other[1]] = {}, [other[2]] = {}, [other[3]] = {} },
			})
		end

		local frames: { { time: number, transforms: { CFrame } } } = {}
		local missed, worst, softened = 0, 0, 0
		local missedFrom, missedTo = math.huge, -math.huge
		for frame = firstFrame, lastFrame do
			local time = frame / rate
			local transforms = transformsAt(channels, time)
			local placed = Pose.place(scan, transforms, identity)
			local current = { transforms[chain[1]], transforms[chain[2]], transforms[chain[3]] }
			local anchor = anchorOf(placed)
			local tip = anchor * tipLocal
			-- On a moving floor, as for a cycle made on the spot: the held point moves on
			-- steadily from where it was at `at`, through the blends too, so a foot eased
			-- in is already moving with the floor when it lands, and one eased out leaves
			-- with it.
			local moved = Roblox.Vector3.new()
			if travel then
				moved = travel * (time - (operation.at or from))
			end
			if rolling then
				local along = smoothstep((time - from) / math.max(to - from, 1e-6))
				local angle = rollFrom + (rollTo - rollFrom) * along
				local turned = heldTurn * Roblox.CFrame.Angles(lift * angle, 0, 0)
				tip = anchor * Roblox.CFrame.new(pointLocal + moved) * turned * Roblox.CFrame.new(-offset)
			elseif travel then
				tip = anchor * (tipLocal + moved)
			end
			local weight = 1
			if time < from - Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
				weight = smoothstep((time - first) / math.max(from - first, 1e-6))
			elseif time > to + Store.TIME_TOLERANCE then
				weight = smoothstep((last - time) / math.max(last - to, 1e-6))
			end
			-- Easing in or out, the target itself moves from where the animation has the part
			-- to where it is held, and the limb reaches for it. The part then travels straight
			-- between the two, instead of wherever angles part way between would put it.
			local free = placed[chain[3]]
			if weight < 1 then
				tip = free:Lerp(tip, weight)
			end
			-- Where the point is beyond the limb's reach, the hips go straight down by
			-- just enough for it to be reached; the limbs named in keep are turned to stay
			-- where they were.
			local drop = 0
			if operation.fit_hips and weight > 0 then
				local upper = Limb.upperOf(placed[Rig.R15_PARENTS[chain[1]]], limb[1], current[1])
				local reach = Limb.fullest(limb, current) * (1 - (operation.soft or 0)) - 1e-4
				local away = upper - Limb.pivotOf(limb[3], tip)
				if away.Magnitude > reach then
					local room = away.Y * away.Y - away:Dot(away) + reach * reach
					drop = math.max(0, if room >= 0 then away.Y - math.sqrt(room) else away.Y)
				end
				if drop > 0 then
					local before = placed
					transforms = table.clone(transforms)
					transforms.LowerTorso = Roblox.CFrame.new(hipsUp * -drop) * transforms.LowerTorso
					placed = Pose.place(scan, transforms, identity)
					current = { transforms[chain[1]], transforms[chain[2]], transforms[chain[3]] }
					for _, other in keepChains do
						local held = Limb.solve({
							parent = placed[Rig.R15_PARENTS[other.chain[1]]],
							joints = other.limb,
							current = {
								transforms[other.chain[1]],
								transforms[other.chain[2]],
								transforms[other.chain[3]],
							},
							pivot = Limb.pivotOf(other.limb[3], before[other.chain[3]]),
							tip = before[other.chain[3]],
							bend = Limb.BEND[other.part],
						})
						for index, joint in other.chain do
							transforms[joint] = held.transforms[index]
						end
					end
					hipsDropped += 1
					deepest = math.max(deepest, drop)
				end
			end
			drops[frame - firstFrame + 1] = drop
			for _, other in keepChains do
				for _, joint in other.chain do
					other.turns[joint][frame - firstFrame + 1] = transforms[joint]
				end
			end
			local solution = if weight <= 0
				then { transforms = current, miss = 0, beyond = false }
				else Limb.solve({
					parent = placed[Rig.R15_PARENTS[chain[1]]],
					joints = limb,
					current = current,
					pivot = Limb.pivotOf(limb[3], tip),
					tip = if full then tip else nil,
					bend = Limb.BEND[operation.part],
					pole = if poleLocal then anchor * poleLocal else nil,
					poleWeight = weight,
					-- Eased in with the hold, so a limb near full stretch doesn't jump on the
					-- first frame of a blend.
					soft = if operation.soft then operation.soft * weight else nil,
				})
			local result = solution.transforms
			if weight >= 1 and not solution.beyond and solution.miss > 0.001 then
				-- Short of the point only because the reach was softened.
				softened = math.max(softened, solution.miss)
			elseif weight >= 1 and solution.miss > 0.001 then
				missed += 1
				worst = math.max(worst, solution.miss)
				missedFrom = math.min(missedFrom, time)
				missedTo = math.max(missedTo, time)
			end
			table.insert(frames, { time = time, transforms = result })
		end

		-- The three joints' rotation keys in the range are replaced by one key a frame.
		for index, joint in chain do
			local turns = {}
			for frame, entry in frames do
				turns[frame] = entry.transforms[index]
			end
			writeTurns(clip, joint, channels[joint] or {}, firstFrame, lastFrame, turns, duration, changed, false)
		end
		if hipsDropped > 0 then
			-- The hips' position, lowered where it had to be, and the limbs kept still.
			local own = channels.LowerTorso or {}
			for axis, letter in { "x", "y", "z" } do
				local share = ({ hipsUp.X, hipsUp.Y, hipsUp.Z })[axis]
				if math.abs(share) < 1e-9 then
					continue
				end
				local channel = `position.{letter}`
				local original = own[channel] or {}
				local values = {}
				for index, drop in drops do
					values[index] = Store.evaluate(original, (firstFrame + index - 1) / rate) - drop * share
				end
				writeFrames(clip, "LowerTorso", channel, original, {
					first = firstFrame,
					last = lastFrame,
					values = values,
					duration = duration,
				}, changed)
			end
			for _, other in keepChains do
				for _, joint in other.chain do
					writeTurns(
						clip,
						joint,
						channels[joint] or {},
						firstFrame,
						lastFrame,
						other.turns[joint],
						duration,
						changed,
						false
					)
				end
			end
			count(changed, "frames_hips_lowered", hipsDropped)
			changed.largest_hip_drop_studs = math.max(changed.largest_hip_drop_studs or 0, rounded(deepest, 3))
		end
		count(changed, "frames_pinned", #frames)
		if softened > 0 then
			changed.largest_soft_studs = math.max(changed.largest_soft_studs or 0, rounded(softened, 3))
		end
		if missed > 0 then
			count(changed, "frames_out_of_reach", missed)
			changed.largest_miss_studs = math.max(changed.largest_miss_studs or 0, rounded(worst, 3))
			-- When, so the hips can be fixed there: the first and last frame out of reach.
			changed.out_of_reach_from = math.min(changed.out_of_reach_from or math.huge, milliseconds(missedFrom))
			changed.out_of_reach_to = math.max(changed.out_of_reach_to or -math.huge, milliseconds(missedTo))
		end
	end,
}

return Ops

--!strict
-- VgaSink.lua -- dirty-rectangle presenter for a Vga device.
--
-- The core owns no Roblox types. A host supplies present(pixels, width, height,
-- rect); the Roblox adapter turns that into an EditableImage write, while the
-- Lune harness can save a PPM or inspect the buffer.

const VgaSink = {}
VgaSink.__index = VgaSink

export type Rect = {
	x: number,
	y: number,
	width: number,
	height: number,
}

export type Present = (pixels: buffer, width: number, height: number, rect: Rect) -> ()

export type VgaSink = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		vga: any,
		present: Present,
		frames: number,
		lastRect: Rect?,
		lastPixels: buffer?,
		poll: (self: VgaSink, force: boolean?) -> boolean,
		invalidate: (self: VgaSink) -> (),
	},
	VgaSink
))

function VgaSink.new(vga: any, present: Present?): VgaSink
	local self = setmetatable({
		vga = vga,
		present = present
			or function(_pixels: buffer, _width: number, _height: number, _rect: Rect) end,
		frames = 0,
		lastRect = nil,
		lastPixels = nil,
	}, VgaSink) :: any
	return self
end

function VgaSink.invalidate(self: VgaSink)
	self.vga:markAllDirty()
end

-- Present only when the VGA has a dirty rectangle, or when force is set. The
-- region snapshot preserves pixels outside the rectangle from prior frames.
function VgaSink.poll(self: VgaSink, force: boolean?): boolean
	local rect: Rect? = self.vga:consumeDirty()
	if not rect and not force then
		return false
	end
	const activeRect: Rect = rect
		or {
			x = 0,
			y = 0,
			width = self.vga:width() :: number,
			height = self.vga:height() :: number,
		}
	const pixels =
		self.vga:snapshotRegionRGBA(activeRect.x, activeRect.y, activeRect.width, activeRect.height)
	self.present(pixels, self.vga:width() :: number, self.vga:height() :: number, activeRect)
	self.frames += 1
	self.lastRect = activeRect
	self.lastPixels = pixels
	return true
end

return VgaSink

local __BENCH_T0__ = os.clock()

local FIB_N = 26000 -- iterations of the Fibonacci loop (6 instr each)
local MIX_N = 26000 -- iterations of the mixing loop (~15 instr each)

-- Opcode numbers
local HALT, LOADK, LOADN, MOV = 1, 2, 3, 4
local ADD, SUB, MUL, ADDI, MODI = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
local AND, OR, XOR, SHL, SHR = 10, 11, 12, 13, 14
local JMP, JLT, JLE, JEQ, JNE = 15, 16, 17, 18, 19
local CALL, RET = 20, 21
local LOAD, STORE = 22, 23

local MOD32 = 4294967296 -- 2^32
local MOD24 = 16777216 -- 2^24

-- Tiny assembler: emits a flat code array (4 slots per instruction)
-- and resolves string labels to absolute pc values in a second pass.
local function newAsm()
	local a = { code = {}, labels = {}, fixups = {} }

	function a.label(name: string)
		a.labels[name] = #a.code + 1
	end

	-- Branch/CALL targets may be passed as label strings.
	function a.emit(op: number, x: any, y: any, z: any)
		local code = a.code
		local base = #code
		code[base + 1] = op
		for i, v in { x or 0, y or 0, z or 0 } do
			if type(v) == "string" then
				table.insert(a.fixups, { base + 1 + i, v })
				code[base + 1 + i] = 0
			else
				code[base + 1 + i] = v
			end
		end
	end

	function a.done()
		for _, f in a.fixups do
			local pc = a.labels[f[2]]
			assert(pc ~= nil, "undefined label: " .. f[2])
			a.code[f[1]] = pc
		end
		return a.code
	end

	return a
end

-- The VM. Closure-based dispatch: every opcode is a closure sharing
-- the registers/heap/pc upvalues. Returns (R[1], instruction count).
local function runVM(code: { number }, consts: { number }, heapSize: number): (number, number)
	local R = table.create(16, 0) -- registers 1..16
	local heap = table.create(heapSize, 0) -- VM heap, addresses 1..heapSize
	local stack = {} -- return-address stack
	local sp = 0
	local pc = 1
	local running = true

	local ops = table.create(23)
	ops[HALT] = function()
		running = false
	end
	ops[LOADK] = function(r, k)
		R[r] = consts[k]
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[LOADN] = function(r, n)
		R[r] = n
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[MOV] = function(r, s)
		R[r] = R[s]
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[ADD] = function(r, x, y)
		R[r] = (R[x] + R[y]) % MOD32
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[SUB] = function(r, x, y)
		R[r] = (R[x] - R[y]) % MOD32
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[MUL] = function(r, x, y) -- 24-bit modular multiply (exact in doubles)
		R[r] = (R[x] % MOD24) * (R[y] % MOD24) % MOD24
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[ADDI] = function(r, x, imm)
		R[r] = (R[x] + imm) % MOD32
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[MODI] = function(r, x, imm)
		R[r] = R[x] % imm
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[AND] = function(r, x, y)
		R[r] = bit32.band(R[x], R[y])
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[OR] = function(r, x, y)
		R[r] = bit32.bor(R[x], R[y])
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[XOR] = function(r, x, y)
		R[r] = bit32.bxor(R[x], R[y])
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[SHL] = function(r, x, imm)
		R[r] = bit32.lshift(R[x], imm)
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[SHR] = function(r, x, imm)
		R[r] = bit32.rshift(R[x], imm)
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[JMP] = function(t)
		pc = t
	end
	ops[JLT] = function(x, y, t)
		pc = if R[x] < R[y] then t else pc + 4
	end
	ops[JLE] = function(x, y, t)
		pc = if R[x] <= R[y] then t else pc + 4
	end
	ops[JEQ] = function(x, y, t)
		pc = if R[x] == R[y] then t else pc + 4
	end
	ops[JNE] = function(x, y, t)
		pc = if R[x] ~= R[y] then t else pc + 4
	end
	ops[CALL] = function(t)
		sp += 1
		stack[sp] = pc + 4
		pc = t
	end
	ops[RET] = function()
		pc = stack[sp]
		sp -= 1
	end
	ops[LOAD] = function(r, aReg) -- R[r] = heap[R[aReg]] (1-based address)
		R[r] = heap[R[aReg]]
		pc += 4
	end
	ops[STORE] = function(aReg, r) -- heap[R[aReg]] = R[r]
		heap[R[aReg]] = R[r]
		pc += 4
	end

	local icount = 0
	while running do
		local p = pc
		ops[code[p]](code[p + 1], code[p + 2], code[p + 3])
		icount += 1
	end
	return R[1], icount
end

-- Program 1 (correctness check): sum of 1..5 via a loop,
-- then CALL a subroutine that stores the sum at heap[3], loads it
-- back and adds 2.  Hand-computed result: (1+2+3+4+5) + 2 = 17.
local function buildCheckProgram()
	local A = newAsm()
	A.emit(LOADN, 1, 0) -- r1 = sum = 0
	A.emit(LOADN, 2, 1) -- r2 = i = 1
	A.emit(LOADN, 3, 6) -- r3 = limit
	A.label("loop")
	A.emit(ADD, 1, 1, 2) -- sum += i
	A.emit(ADDI, 2, 2, 1) -- i += 1
	A.emit(JLT, 2, 3, "loop")
	A.emit(CALL, "bump")
	A.emit(HALT)
	A.label("bump") -- heap[3] = sum; sum = heap[3] + 2
	A.emit(LOADN, 4, 3) -- r4 = address 3
	A.emit(STORE, 4, 1)
	A.emit(LOAD, 5, 4) -- r5 = heap[3]
	A.emit(LOADN, 6, 2)
	A.emit(ADD, 1, 5, 6)
	A.emit(RET)
	return A.done()
end

do
	local result, icount = runVM(buildCheckProgram(), {}, 8)
	assert(result == 17, "VM check: expected 17, got " .. result)
	-- 3 setup + 5*3 loop + CALL + 6 subroutine + HALT = 26 instructions
	assert(icount == 26, "VM check: expected 26 instructions, got " .. icount)
end

-- Program 2: Fibonacci mod 2^24, then the heap-mixing loop
-- with a CALLed mix subroutine, then a heap-summing pass.
local function buildMainProgram(fibN: number, mixN: number)
	local A = newAsm()

	-- Phase A: r2 = fib(fibN) mod 2^24
	A.emit(LOADN, 1, 0) -- r1 = a
	A.emit(LOADN, 2, 1) -- r2 = b
	A.emit(LOADN, 3, 0) -- r3 = i
	A.emit(LOADK, 4, 1) -- r4 = fibN (from constant pool)
	A.label("fib")
	A.emit(ADD, 5, 1, 2) -- r5 = a + b
	A.emit(MODI, 5, 5, MOD24)
	A.emit(MOV, 1, 2)
	A.emit(MOV, 2, 5)
	A.emit(ADDI, 3, 3, 1)
	A.emit(JLT, 3, 4, "fib")

	-- Phase B: mixing loop over a 64-slot heap region
	A.emit(LOADN, 3, 0) -- r3 = i
	A.emit(LOADK, 4, 2) -- r4 = mixN
	A.emit(LOADN, 6, 12345) -- r6 = acc
	A.label("mix")
	A.emit(MODI, 7, 3, 64) -- r7 = i % 64
	A.emit(ADDI, 7, 7, 1) -- 1-based heap address
	A.emit(CALL, "mixsub")
	A.emit(STORE, 7, 6) -- heap[r7] = acc
	A.emit(LOAD, 8, 7) -- r8 = heap[r7]
	A.emit(XOR, 6, 6, 8) -- fold back (== 0 here, keeps acc bounded? no:
	A.emit(OR, 6, 6, 8) --   XOR zeroes acc, OR restores it -- both exercised)
	A.emit(ADDI, 3, 3, 1)
	A.emit(JLT, 3, 4, "mix")
	A.emit(JMP, "sum")

	A.label("mixsub") -- acc = mix(acc, i)
	A.emit(XOR, 6, 6, 3)
	A.emit(MUL, 9, 6, 6) -- low-24-bit square
	A.emit(ADD, 6, 6, 9)
	A.emit(SHR, 10, 6, 7)
	A.emit(XOR, 6, 6, 10)
	A.emit(SHL, 10, 6, 3)
	A.emit(XOR, 6, 6, 10)
	A.emit(RET)

	-- Phase C: sum the heap, combine with fib value and acc into r1
	A.label("sum")
	A.emit(LOADN, 3, 1) -- r3 = address
	A.emit(LOADN, 4, 65) -- r4 = limit
	A.emit(LOADN, 11, 0) -- r11 = total
	A.label("sl")
	A.emit(LOAD, 8, 3)
	A.emit(ADD, 11, 11, 8)
	A.emit(ADDI, 3, 3, 1)
	A.emit(JLT, 3, 4, "sl")
	A.emit(XOR, 1, 2, 6) -- r1 = fib ^ acc
	A.emit(ADD, 1, 1, 11) -- r1 += heap total (mod 2^32)
	A.emit(HALT)

	return A.done(), { fibN, mixN }
end

-- Bulk workload
local mainCode, mainConsts = buildMainProgram(FIB_N, MIX_N)

local t0 = os.clock()
local result, icount = runVM(mainCode, mainConsts, 64)
local elapsed = os.clock() - t0

-- checksum folds the VM result together with the executed-instruction
-- count, so both must reproduce exactly
local checksum = (result * 65599 + icount) % 4294967296

local EXPECTED = 2159502503 -- baked in from a reference run (icount 598270)
assert(checksum == EXPECTED, "bytecode_vm checksum mismatch: " .. checksum .. " (icount " .. icount .. ")")

print(string.format("bytecode_vm checksum: %s", tostring(checksum)))
print("main work time", elapsed * 1000)
print("entire script time", (os.clock() - __BENCH_T0__) * 1000)

--!strict
-- Reading a curve clip for the tools, and the lines its fingerprint is made from.

local Need = require("./Need")
local Store = require("./Store")

local currentBackend = Store.currentBackend
local milliseconds = Need.milliseconds
local outward = Store.outward
local rounded = Need.rounded

local Read = {}

export type ReadOptions = {
	joints: { string }?,
	timeFrom: number?,
	timeTo: number?,
	offset: number?,
	limit: number?,
	posesOnly: boolean?,
}

function Read.read(clip: Instance, options: ReadOptions): { [string]: any }
	local result: { [string]: any } = {}
	local tracks = Store.tracks(clip)
	local function within(time: number): boolean
		return not (
			(options.timeFrom and time < options.timeFrom - Store.TIME_TOLERANCE)
			or (options.timeTo and time > options.timeTo + Store.TIME_TOLERANCE)
		)
	end
	if not options.posesOnly then
		local animated: { [string]: boolean } = {}
		local keyCount = 0
		for _, track in tracks do
			local keys = Store.keys(track.curve)
			keyCount += #keys
			if #keys > 0 then
				animated[track.joint] = true
			end
		end
		local joints = {}
		for name in animated do
			table.insert(joints, name)
		end
		table.sort(joints)
		local times = {}
		local allTimes = Store.keyTimes(clip)
		local matching = 0
		for _, time in allTimes do
			if within(time) then
				matching += 1
				if #times < Store.MAX_LISTED then
					table.insert(times, milliseconds(time))
				end
			end
		end
		local markers = {}
		for _, curve in Store.markerCurves(clip) do
			for _, marker in currentBackend().markers(curve) do
				if within(marker.time) and #markers < Store.MAX_LISTED then
					table.insert(markers, { name = curve.Name, value = marker.value, time = milliseconds(marker.time) })
				end
			end
		end
		table.sort(markers, function(a, b)
			return a.time < b.time
		end)
		result.format = "curves"
		result.name = clip.Name
		result.loop = (clip :: any).Loop
		result.priority = (clip :: any).Priority.Name
		result.duration = milliseconds(Store.duration(clip))
		result.keyframe_count = #allTimes
		result.keyframe_times = times
		result.keyframe_times_truncated = if matching > #times then true else nil
		result.key_count = keyCount
		result.animated_joints = joints
		result.markers = markers
	end
	local wanted: { string } = options.joints or {}
	if #wanted > 0 then
		local offset = math.max(0, math.floor(options.offset or 0))
		local limit = math.clamp(math.floor(options.limit or Store.DEFAULT_KEYS), 1, Store.MAX_PAGE)
		local page, total = {}, 0
		for _, joint: string in wanted :: { string } do
			for _, channel in Store.CHANNELS do
				local curve = Store.channel(clip, joint, channel, false)
				if curve then
					local scale = outward(channel)
					for _, key in Store.keys(curve) do
						if within(key.time) then
							total += 1
							if total > offset and #page < limit then
								table.insert(page, {
									joint = joint,
									channel = channel,
									time = milliseconds(key.time),
									value = rounded(key.value * scale, 4),
									interpolation = key.interpolation,
									["in"] = if key.left ~= nil then rounded(key.left * scale, 3) else nil,
									out = if key.right ~= nil then rounded(key.right * scale, 3) else nil,
								})
							end
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
		result.keys = page
		result.keys_total = total
		if offset + #page < total then
			result.next_offset = offset + #page
		end
	end
	return result
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Fingerprint lines and checks

local function nine(value: number?): string
	return if value == nil then "-" else string.format("%.9g", value)
end

-- One line for everything in the clip that affects how it plays, in a fixed order.
function Read.digestLines(clip: Instance): { string }
	local lines = { `loop|{tostring((clip :: any).Loop)}`, `priority|{tostring((clip :: any).Priority)}` }
	for _, track in Store.tracks(clip) do
		for _, key in Store.keys(track.curve) do
			table.insert(
				lines,
				`key|{track.path}|{nine(key.time)}|{nine(key.value)}|{key.interpolation}|{nine(key.left)}|{nine(
					key.right
				)}`
			)
		end
	end
	for _, curve in Store.markerCurves(clip) do
		for _, marker in currentBackend().markers(curve) do
			table.insert(lines, `marker|{curve.Name}|{nine(marker.time)}|{marker.value}`)
		end
	end
	table.sort(lines)
	return lines
end

return Read

--!strict
-- Xms.lua -- minimal XMS 3.0 driver (HIMEM entry point, A20, HMA, EMB moves).
-- WIN.CNF probes INT 2Fh AX=4300/4310 and then calls the far entry; DOSX uses
-- the same interface after the CPU/version gate. No HIMEM.SYS binary needed.

const band, bor, lshift, rshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift, bit32.rshift

const Xms = {}
Xms.__index = Xms

-- Reserved hypervisor segment: F100 hosts the IVT/timer/mouse stubs up to
-- 0x6D, so the XMS far entry goes at 0xC0 and cannot overlap a loaded program
-- (the DOS loader places images below the 0xA000 arena top, but a segment as
-- low as F200 looked "free" only until WSWAP happened to land there).
const ENTRY_SEG = 0xF100
const ENTRY_OFF = 0x00C0
const HMA_START = 0x100000
const HMA_SIZE = 0x10000
const EXT_START = HMA_START + HMA_SIZE

export type Block = {
	start: number,
	size: number,
}

export type Xms = {
	machine: any,
	a20: boolean,
	hmaInUse: boolean,
	blocks: { [number]: Block },
	nextHandle: number,
	entrySeg: number,
	entryOff: number,
	FN: { [number]: (self: Xms, cpu: any) -> () },
	enabled: (self: Xms) -> boolean,
	int2f: (self: Xms) -> boolean,
	dispatch: (self: Xms) -> (),
	releaseAll: (self: Xms) -> (),
}

function Xms.new(machine: any): Xms
	const self = setmetatable({}, Xms) :: any
	self.machine = machine
	-- HIMEM.SYS enables A20 while it initialises and leaves it on; real DOS
	-- extended-memory users (WSWAP) rely on that. 8086 keeps the 20-bit wrap.
	self.a20 = machine.cpu.level >= 1
	machine.mem.a20 = self.a20
	self.hmaInUse = false
	self.blocks = {}
	self.nextHandle = 1
	self.entrySeg = ENTRY_SEG
	self.entryOff = ENTRY_OFF
	-- Far entry: INT 9Fh (inline-dispatched by the machine's stub) ; RETF.
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF, 0xCD)
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF + 1, 0x9F)
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF + 2, 0xCB)
	-- The no-ROM test/hypervisor machine installs every IVT vector as a far
	-- return at F000:0100. Hook the two DPMI-era services here so INT 2Fh and
	-- the far XMS entry reach the driver without a DOS layer.
	machine.cpu.defaultInts[0x2F] = function()
		self:int2f()
	end
	machine.cpu.defaultInts[0x9F] = function()
		self:dispatch()
	end
	machine.cpu:registerStub(0x2F, 0xF000, 0x0100)
	machine.cpu:registerStub(0x9F, 0xF000, 0x0100)
	return self
end

function Xms.enabled(self: Xms): boolean
	return self.machine.cpu.level >= 1 -- 286+
end

-- INT 2Fh installation check / driver entry. Returns true when handled.
function Xms.int2f(self: Xms): boolean
	const cpu = self.machine.cpu
	if not self:enabled() then
		return false
	end
	const ax = cpu.r[1]
	if ax == 0x4300 then
		cpu:wb(0, 0x80)
		cpu:wr(3, 0x0100)
		return true
	elseif ax == 0x4310 then
		cpu.es = self.entrySeg
		cpu:wr(3, self.entryOff)
		return true
	end
	return false
end

local function setMemA20(self: Xms, on: boolean)
	self.a20 = on
	self.machine.mem.a20 = on
end

local function freeList(self: Xms): { Block }
	local list: { Block } = {}
	for _, block in pairs(self.blocks) do
		list[#list + 1] = block
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a: Block, b: Block): boolean
		return a.start < b.start
	end)
	return list
end

local function memoryTotals(self: Xms): (number, number)
	const memSize = self.machine.mem.size
	local cursor = EXT_START
	local largest, total = 0, 0
	for _, block in ipairs(freeList(self)) do
		const gap = block.start - cursor
		if gap > largest then
			largest = gap
		end
		total += gap
		cursor = block.start + block.size
	end
	const tail = memSize - cursor
	if tail > largest then
		largest = tail
	end
	total += tail
	return math.floor(largest / 1024), math.floor(total / 1024)
end

local function allocate(self: Xms, bytes: number): (number?, number?)
	local cursor = EXT_START
	const memSize = self.machine.mem.size
	for _, block in ipairs(freeList(self)) do
		if block.start - cursor >= bytes then
			const handle = self.nextHandle
			self.nextHandle += 1
			self.blocks[handle] = { start = cursor, size = bytes }
			return handle, cursor
		end
		cursor = block.start + block.size
	end
	if memSize - cursor >= bytes then
		const handle = self.nextHandle
		self.nextHandle += 1
		self.blocks[handle] = { start = cursor, size = bytes }
		return handle, cursor
	end
	return nil, nil
end

local function readDword(mem: any, addr: number): number
	return bor(mem:read16(addr), lshift(mem:read16(addr + 2), 16))
end

local function copyLinear(mem: any, dst: number, src: number, length: number)
	for index = 0, length - 1 do
		mem:write8(dst + index, mem:read8(src + index))
	end
end

Xms.FN = {}

Xms.FN[0x00] = function(_self: Xms, cpu: any) -- get version
	cpu:wr(0, 0x0300)
	cpu:wr(3, 0x0100)
end

Xms.FN[0x01] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- request HMA (DX = KB)
	if self.hmaInUse then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	self.hmaInUse = true
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x02] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- release HMA
	self.hmaInUse = false
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x03] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- enable A20
	setMemA20(self, true)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x04] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- disable A20
	setMemA20(self, false)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x05] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- local enable A20
	setMemA20(self, true)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x06] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- local disable A20
	setMemA20(self, false)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x07] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query A20
	cpu:wr(0, self.a20 and 1 or 0)
end

Xms.FN[0x08] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query free memory
	const largest, total = memoryTotals(self)
	cpu:wr(0, largest)
	cpu:wr(2, total)
end

Xms.FN[0x09] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- allocate EMB (DX = KB)
	const handle = allocate(self, cpu.r[3] * 1024)
	if not handle then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(2, handle) -- XMS 09: DX = handle, AX = 1
end

Xms.FN[0x0A] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- free EMB
	if self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] then
		self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] = nil
		cpu:wr(0, 1)
	else
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
	end
end

Xms.FN[0x0B] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- move extended memory block
	const mem = self.machine.mem
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[7] -- DS:SI -> move structure
	const length = readDword(mem, base)
	const srcHandle = mem:read16(base + 4)
	const srcOffset = readDword(mem, base + 6)
	const dstHandle = mem:read16(base + 10)
	const dstOffset = readDword(mem, base + 12)
	-- XMS 0Bh: handle 0 means a real-mode segment:offset packed as a DWORD
	-- (segment in the high word), not a linear address. WSWAP depends on it.
	local function realAddress(offset: number): number
		return lshift(rshift(offset, 16), 4) + band(offset, 0xFFFF)
	end
	local src
	local dst
	if srcHandle == 0 then
		src = realAddress(srcOffset)
	else
		const block = self.blocks[srcHandle]
		if not block or srcOffset + length > block.size then
			cpu:wr(0, 0)
			return
		end
		src = block.start + srcOffset
	end
	if dstHandle == 0 then
		dst = realAddress(dstOffset)
	else
		const block = self.blocks[dstHandle]
		if not block or dstOffset + length > block.size then
			cpu:wr(0, 0)
			return
		end
		dst = block.start + dstOffset
	end
	-- XMS owns A20 during a move: the guest's current gate state must not fold
	-- destinations that live in extended memory (DOSX disables A20 while it
	-- prepares its GDT, then copies the table into an EMB with 0Bh).
	const savedA20 = mem.a20
	mem.a20 = true
	copyLinear(mem, dst, src, length)
	mem.a20 = savedA20
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x0C] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- lock EMB
	const block = self.blocks[cpu.r[3]]
	if not block then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(3, band(block.start, 0xFFFF))
	cpu:wr(2, band(rshift(block.start, 16), 0xFFFF))
end

Xms.FN[0x0D] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- unlock EMB
	cpu:wr(0, self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] and 1 or 0)
end

Xms.FN[0x0E] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- get EMB info
	const block = self.blocks[cpu.r[3]]
	if not block then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(3, 0) -- BL=0 locked blocks, BH=0 total blocks
	cpu:wr(2, band(block.size / 1024, 0xFFFF)) -- DX = size KB
end

Xms.FN[0x88] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query any extended memory
	const kb = math.floor((self.machine.mem.size - HMA_START) / 1024)
	cpu:wr(0, band(kb, 0xFFFF))
end

Xms.FN[0x89] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- allocate any extended memory
	const handle = allocate(self, cpu.r[3] * 1024)
	if not handle then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(2, handle)
end

-- A new image cannot inherit another process's extended-memory handles. Real
-- DOS leaves them allocated, but Windows 3.1's WSWAP keeps its swap block and
-- returns to WIN.CNF without freeing it, which would leave DOSX with no XMS.
-- Releasing on EXEC matches what a well-behaved DOS session needs.
function Xms.releaseAll(self: Xms)
	self.blocks = {}
	self.hmaInUse = false
end

function Xms.dispatch(self: Xms)
	const cpu = self.machine.cpu
	const fn = band(rshift(cpu.r[1], 8), 0xFF)
	const handler = self.FN[fn]
	if not handler then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	handler(self, cpu)
end

return Xms

-- aliasing: tables are shared, strings are values
local shared = { n = 0 }
local function bump(t) t.n = t.n + 1 end
bump(shared); bump(shared)
print(shared.n)

local a = shared
a.n = 42
print(shared.n)

local s1 = "abc"
local s2 = s1
s1 = s1 .. "d"
print(s1, s2)

local deep = { list = { 1, 2, 3 }, meta = { tag = "root" } }
local function clone(t)
  local out = {}
  for k, v in pairs(t) do
    if type(v) == "table" then out[k] = clone(v) else out[k] = v end
  end
  return out
end
local copy = clone(deep)
copy.list[2] = 99
copy.meta.tag = "copy"
print(deep.list[2], copy.list[2], deep.meta.tag, copy.meta.tag)

local function swap(t, i, j) t[i], t[j] = t[j], t[i] end
local arr = { "a", "b", "c" }
swap(arr, 1, 3)
print(table.concat(arr, ","))

-- closure capture of a table sees later writes
local box = { v = 1 }
local peek = function() return box.v end
box.v = 7
print(peek())

--!strict
-- Ranges across a loop's seam. In a looping clip the end and the start are one moment, so
-- an operation whose range, or a blend of it, reaches either end has to change both alike,
-- and a range may run on past the end and round from the start: time_from after time_to,
-- as a step that lands just after the loop begins. Such an operation is run on the loop
-- started elsewhere, where its range lies whole inside it, and the loop is then started
-- where it was again. Starting a loop elsewhere cuts the curves exactly (Write.wrapped),
-- so the motion is the same; each channel the operation left alone is then put back key
-- for key, and the cut left in a channel it changed is taken out where it can be exactly.

local Frames = require("./Frames")
local Need = require("./Need")
local Store = require("./Store")
local Write = require("./Write")

type Key = Store.Key
type Context = Frames.Context
type Changed = Frames.Changed
export type Apply = (where: string, clip: Instance, operation: any, context: Context, changed: Changed) -> ()

local milliseconds = Need.milliseconds
local rounded = Need.rounded
local refuse = Need.refuse

local Seam = {}

-- How much of a loop a range across its seam must leave out, in frames: room for the cut
-- where the loop is started while the operation runs, and a frame either side of it.
local ROOM = 3

local function sameKey(a: Key, b: Key): boolean
	return math.abs(a.time - b.time) < Store.TIME_TOLERANCE
		and a.value == b.value
		and a.interpolation == b.interpolation
		and a.left == b.left
		and a.right == b.right
end

local function sameKeys(a: { Key }, b: { Key }): boolean
	if #a ~= #b then
		return false
	end
	for index, key in a do
		if not sameKey(key, b[index]) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function startElsewhere(clip: Instance, offset: number, duration: number)
	for _, track in Store.tracks(clip) do
		local keys = Store.keys(track.curve)
		if #keys > 0 then
			Store.setKeys(track.curve, Write.wrapped(keys, offset, duration))
		end
	end
end

-- The cut at `time` taken out of a channel, where the keys either side of it are the
-- channel's own as they were: the stretch between them is then the one it always was.
local function withoutCut(keys: { Key }, original: { Key }, time: number): { Key }
	local tolerance = Store.TIME_TOLERANCE
	local function own(key: Key?): boolean
		if not key then
			return false
		end
		for _, before in original do
			if sameKey(before, key) then
				return true
			end
		end
		return false
	end
	for _, before in original do
		if math.abs(before.time - time) < tolerance then
			return keys
		end
	end
	for index, key in keys do
		if math.abs(key.time - time) < tolerance then
			if own(keys[index - 1]) and own(keys[index + 1]) then
				local out = table.clone(keys)
				table.remove(out, index)
				return out
			end
			return keys
		end
	end
	return keys
end

-- What an operation reports, added to what the batch has reported so far, its times
-- given back on the loop as it was: counts add up, a largest keeps the largest, a time
-- where something begins (_from, _at) keeps the first and one where it ends (_to) the last;
-- anything else is replaced.
local function merge(changed: Changed, found: Changed, timeOf: (number) -> number)
	for name, value in found do
		local begins = string.sub(name, -5) == "_from" or string.sub(name, -3) == "_at"
		local ends = string.sub(name, -3) == "_to"
		if begins or ends then
			value = timeOf(value)
		end
		local before = changed[name]
		if before == nil then
			changed[name] = value
		elseif string.sub(name, 1, 8) == "largest_" or ends then
			changed[name] = math.max(before, value)
		elseif begins then
			changed[name] = math.min(before, value)
		elseif string.sub(name, 1, 7) == "travel_" then
			changed[name] = value
		else
			changed[name] = before + value
		end
	end
end

-- Runs `apply` for an operation with a range (time_from, time_to and any blend_in,
-- blend_out and at), across the seam of a looping clip where its range reaches it.
function Seam.apply(where: string, clip: Instance, operation: any, context: Context, changed: Changed, apply: Apply)
	local from, to = operation.time_from, operation.time_to
	local across = to < from
	local looping = (clip :: any).Loop == true
	if not looping then
		if across then
			refuse(
				where,
				"time_to is before time_from. A range runs on past the end and round from the start only in a looping clip."
			)
		end
		apply(where, clip, operation, context, changed)
		return
	end
	local duration = Store.duration(clip)
	local tolerance = Store.TIME_TOLERANCE
	local rate = Store.FRAME_RATE
	local reach = if across then to + duration else to
	local first = from - (operation.blend_in or 0)
	local last = reach + (operation.blend_out or 0)
	local whole = not across and Frames.near(from, 0) and Frames.near(to, duration)
	local inside = first > tolerance and last < duration - tolerance
	-- A range past the end is left to the operation to refuse, in its own words.
	if whole or inside or to > duration + tolerance then
		apply(where, clip, operation, context, changed)
		return
	end
	if from > duration + tolerance then
		refuse(where, `the clip ends at {milliseconds(duration)} seconds, before time_from.`)
	end
	local frames = duration * rate
	if math.abs(frames - math.round(frames)) > Frames.FRAME_SLACK then
		refuse(
			where,
			"the range reaches the end of the loop, but the loop is not a whole number of frames long, so its end and start cannot be lined up.",
			"Key the loop's end on a whole frame."
		)
	end
	if last - first > duration - ROOM / rate + tolerance then
		refuse(
			where,
			`the range with its blends spans {milliseconds(last - first)} seconds, too much of the {milliseconds(
				duration
			)}-second loop to run across its end.`,
			`Leave at least {milliseconds(ROOM / rate)} seconds of the loop out, or use the whole loop: 0 to {milliseconds(
				duration
			)} seconds.`
		)
	end

	-- The loop must close: each channel ending where it starts. A loop that doesn't, such
	-- as one turning from 0 to 360 degrees, can't have its end joined to its start without
	-- changing its motion, which the operation would then be worked out from.
	for _, track in Store.tracks(clip) do
		local keys = Store.keys(track.curve)
		if #keys > 0 then
			local opening, closing = Store.evaluate(keys, 0), Store.evaluate(keys, duration)
			if math.abs(opening - closing) > 1e-3 then
				refuse(
					where,
					`the range reaches the end of the loop, but the loop doesn't close: {track.joint} {track.channel} starts at {rounded(
						opening,
						4
					)} and ends at {rounded(closing, 4)}, so its end can't be joined to its start.`,
					"Close the loop first: copy_pose from 0 to its end."
				)
			end
		end
	end
	-- The loop is cut and joined at its whole number of frames. A loop that ends a little
	-- off a frame (0.667 typed for 20/30 of a second) would otherwise put every key that
	-- comes round the end that little off a frame too. Its stray end key, within a
	-- millisecond of the frame, is taken as the loop's end and put back on the frame. But
	-- only where no other key is that near the frame: a key just before an end that is
	-- just after the frame is a key of its own, and would be lost as the end. Such a loop
	-- is cut at its own length, as it is; keys that come round it may then land a little
	-- off a frame, which validation points out, but no motion is lost.
	local period = math.round(frames) / rate
	for _, track in Store.tracks(clip) do
		local keys = Store.keys(track.curve)
		for index = 1, #keys - 1 do
			if keys[index].time >= period - tolerance then
				period = duration
			end
		end
	end
	-- The loop started so that the range and its blends lie in its middle, on whole frames.
	local offset = math.round((period / 2 - (first + last) / 2) * rate) / rate
	local function onLoop(time: number): number
		local placed = time % period
		return if placed > period - tolerance then placed - period else placed
	end
	local moved = table.clone(operation)
	moved.time_from = from + offset
	moved.time_to = reach + offset
	if operation.at ~= nil then
		moved.at = onLoop(operation.at + offset)
	end

	local own: { [Instance]: { Key } } = {}
	for _, track in Store.tracks(clip) do
		own[track.curve] = Store.keys(track.curve)
	end
	startElsewhere(clip, offset, period)
	local started: { [Instance]: { Key } } = {}
	for curve in own do
		started[curve] = Store.keys(curve)
	end
	local found: Changed = {}
	apply(where, clip, moved, context, found)
	local left: { [Instance]: boolean } = {}
	for curve, keys in started do
		left[curve] = sameKeys(Store.keys(curve), keys)
	end
	startElsewhere(clip, -offset, period)
	-- Where the loop was started while the operation ran; a channel it changed is cut there.
	local cut = onLoop(-offset)
	for curve, keys in own do
		if left[curve] then
			Store.setKeys(curve, keys)
		else
			Store.setKeys(curve, withoutCut(Store.keys(curve), keys, cut))
		end
	end
	merge(changed, found, function(time: number): number
		return milliseconds(onLoop(time - offset))
	end)
end

return Seam

-- UIPageLayout: where its pages are, CurrentPage, the jumps, and Stopped
-- after a turn; positions are read once each turn has settled.
--! client
local player = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local function v(p)
	return string.format("%g,%g", math.round(p.X * 100) / 100 + 0, math.round(p.Y * 100) / 100 + 0)
end
local box = Instance.new("Frame")
box.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(400, 300)
box.Parent = screen
local layout = Instance.new("UIPageLayout")
layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
layout.Animated = false
layout.Parent = box
local pages = {}
for i, s in { { 0.5, 0.5 }, { 1, 1 }, { 0.25, 0.5 }, { 0.5, 0.25 } } do
	local f = Instance.new("Frame")
	f.Name = "P" .. i
	f.LayoutOrder = i
	f.Size = UDim2.fromScale(s[1], s[2])
	f.Parent = box
	pages[i] = f
end
local stopped = {}
layout.Stopped:Connect(function(page)
	table.insert(stopped, page.Name)
end)
local function dump(tag)
	local out = {}
	for _, f in pages do
		table.insert(out, f.Name .. "@" .. v(f.AbsolutePosition - box.AbsolutePosition) .. "/" .. v(f.AbsoluteSize))
	end
	log(tag, tostring(layout.CurrentPage), table.concat(out, " "), "content", v(layout.AbsoluteContentSize))
end

dump("start")
layout:Next()
dump("next")
layout:JumpToIndex(3)
layout:Next()
dump("next at the end")
layout:Previous()
dump("previous")
layout:JumpToIndex(10)
dump("index out of range")
layout:JumpTo(pages[1])
dump("jump to P1")
layout:Previous()
dump("previous at the start")
layout.Circular = true
layout:Previous()
dump("circular previous")
layout.Circular = false
layout.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
layout.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0.1, 0)
dump("centered, padded")
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Vertical
dump("vertical")
pages[3].Visible = false
layout:JumpToIndex(2)
dump("P3 hidden, index 2")
pages[3].Visible = true
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 0)

layout.Animated = true
layout.TweenTime = 0.3
layout:JumpToIndex(1)
log("current at once", layout.CurrentPage)
task.wait(1)
dump("after a turn")
log("stopped", table.concat(stopped, ","))

screen:Destroy()

-- bigint: decimal arithmetic on digit arrays, no floats in the result path
local function normalise(a)
  local i = #a
  while i > 1 and a[i] == 0 do
    a[i] = nil
    i = i - 1
  end
  return a
end
local function fromNumber(n)
  local a = {}
  if n == 0 then return { 0 } end
  while n > 0 do
    a[#a + 1] = n % 10
    n = math.floor(n / 10)
  end
  return a
end
local function add(a, b)
  local out, carry = {}, 0
  for i = 1, math.max(#a, #b) do
    local sum = (a[i] or 0) + (b[i] or 0) + carry
    out[i] = sum % 10
    carry = math.floor(sum / 10)
  end
  if carry > 0 then out[#out + 1] = carry end
  return out
end
local function mul(a, b)
  local out = {}
  for i = 1, #a + #b do out[i] = 0 end
  for i = 1, #a do
    local carry = 0
    for j = 1, #b do
      local cur = out[i + j - 1] + a[i] * b[j] + carry
      out[i + j - 1] = cur % 10
      carry = math.floor(cur / 10)
    end
    local k = i + #b
    while carry > 0 do
      local cur = out[k] + carry
      out[k] = cur % 10
      carry = math.floor(cur / 10)
      k = k + 1
    end
  end
  return normalise(out)
end
local function show(a)
  local out = {}
  for i = #a, 1, -1 do out[#out + 1] = tostring(a[i]) end
  return table.concat(out)
end
local function factorial(n)
  local acc = { 1 }
  for i = 2, n do acc = mul(acc, fromNumber(i)) end
  return acc
end

print(show(add(fromNumber(999999), fromNumber(1))))
print(show(mul(fromNumber(123456789), fromNumber(987654321))))
print(show(factorial(20)))
print(show(factorial(30)))
print(#show(factorial(50)))
local fib1, fib2 = { 1 }, { 1 }
for i = 3, 40 do fib1, fib2 = fib2, add(fib1, fib2) end
print(show(fib2))
